Customer Question: What business outcomes must this Secure Plus engagement achieve?
Why This Must Be Asked: The target architecture and project priorities should be driven by business outcomes rather than by deploying every available Microsoft feature.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Reduce cyber risk; replace third-party tools; modernize endpoints; migrate data; prepare for Copilot; satisfy compliance requirements; reduce support effort
Configuration Impact: Determines project priorities, success criteria, roadmap sequencing and acceptance criteria
Required Participants: Executive Sponsor; Technical Lead; Security Owner; Business Owners
Default If Undecided: Document objectives as unresolved and do not finalize the roadmap
Engineering Notes: Require measurable outcomes wherever possible.

Customer Question: Which platforms, workloads, locations and business units are included in the engagement?
Why This Must Be Asked: Engineers need to know which tenants, environments and workloads can be assessed or changed.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Microsoft Entra; Exchange Online; Exchange Server; SharePoint; Teams; OneDrive; Intune; Defender; Purview; Azure; Active Directory; file servers; Apple devices; Copilot; Copilot Studio
Configuration Impact: Controls which platforms are inventoried, assessed, configured, tested and transitioned to support
Required Participants: Technical Lead; Workload Owners; Project Manager
Default If Undecided: Assess Microsoft 365 tenant only and mark all other environments as not assessed
Engineering Notes: List explicit exclusions rather than relying on implied scope.

Customer Question: Which services, systems, business units or locations must not be assessed or changed?
Why This Must Be Asked: Unclear exclusions can lead to incomplete dependencies or unauthorized configuration changes.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Acquired companies; development tenants; regulated business units; provider-managed servers; third-party SaaS; legacy applications
Configuration Impact: Creates baseline exclusions and identifies areas requiring alternate owners or service providers
Required Participants: Project Manager; Technical Lead; Legal or Compliance Owner
Default If Undecided: Treat undocumented systems as discovery-only with no authorized configuration changes
Engineering Notes: An excluded dependency can still block an in-scope change.

Customer Question: What measurable conditions must be met for each phase to be accepted?
Why This Must Be Asked: Engineers need objective validation criteria for configuration, testing, support handoff and residual risk.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: MFA coverage percentage; device compliance percentage; no high-risk users; approved data owners; tested recovery; signed operational handoff
Configuration Impact: Determines validation tests, evidence requirements and phase acceptance gates
Required Participants: Technical Lead; Security Owner; Workstream Owners
Default If Undecided: Use the Secure Plus standard acceptance criteria and record customer approval as pending
Engineering Notes: Separate configuration completion from operational acceptance.

Customer Question: Who can approve technical configuration, user-impacting changes, risk exceptions and project scope changes?
Why This Must Be Asked: Engineers need to know who is authorized to make each type of decision.
Expected Answer Type: Named person or role per decision type
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Executive Sponsor; Security Owner; CIO; Compliance Officer; Technical Owner; Change Advisory Board
Configuration Impact: Populates the RACI, approval workflows, change process and exception management
Required Participants: Project Manager; Security Owner; Legal or Compliance Owner
Default If Undecided: Escalate decisions to the Executive Sponsor
Engineering Notes: Use named people and backup approvers, not only department names.

Customer Question: Who owns identity, endpoints, messaging, collaboration, data, applications, security, compliance, backup and AI governance?
Why This Must Be Asked: Controls cannot be accepted or operationalized without accountable owners.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Internal IT; security team; compliance team; business data owner; MSP; application vendor
Configuration Impact: Determines approval, testing, operational handoff and review ownership for baseline controls
Required Participants: Department Leaders; Technical Lead; Service Manager
Default If Undecided: Assign an interim owner and record an ownership gap
Engineering Notes: Each major workload should have both a technical operator and accountable business owner where applicable.

Customer Question: What support and escalation coverage is required for security incidents and implementation changes?
Why This Must Be Asked: The answer affects alert routing, change windows, incident response and ongoing service scope.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Business hours only; extended hours; 24x7 critical alerts; 24x7 full operations
Configuration Impact: Determines Phase 4 monitoring commitments, notification targets and escalation SLAs
Required Participants: Security Owner; Service Desk Manager; Executive Sponsor
Default If Undecided: Business-hours coverage with documented boundaries
Engineering Notes: Do not imply 24x7 monitoring when the contracted service does not include it.

Customer Question: Which business units and technical owners must participate in discovery and design sessions?
Why This Must Be Asked: Missing stakeholders can produce technically correct settings that disrupt a business process.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Identity; endpoint; infrastructure; messaging; data; compliance; legal; HR; application owners; service desk; AI governance
Configuration Impact: Determines discovery schedule and required signoffs
Required Participants: Executive Sponsor; Technical Lead; Department Leaders
Default If Undecided: Schedule all standard Secure Plus capability workshops
Engineering Notes: Separate technical assessment sessions from business decision workshops.

Customer Question: How may engineers access the customer tenant and related systems?
Why This Must Be Asked: The access model determines available assessment methods, automation options and evidence quality.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Named cloud accounts; GDAP; PIM-eligible roles; supervised sessions; customer-executed scripts; read-only exports
Configuration Impact: Determines whether engineers can use Microsoft Graph, PowerShell, portals, supervised sessions or customer-generated exports
Required Participants: Technical Lead; Partner Administrator; Compliance Owner
Default If Undecided: Use read-only supervised access or customer-executed exports
Engineering Notes: Prefer least privilege and time-bound access.

Customer Question: Which Microsoft Entra and workload roles may be assigned to the engineering team?
Why This Must Be Asked: Engineers need enough access to assess and configure services without unnecessarily receiving Global Administrator.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Global Reader; Security Reader; Reports Reader; Conditional Access Administrator; Intune Administrator; Exchange Administrator; SharePoint Administrator; Compliance Administrator
Configuration Impact: Determines technical access and whether some steps must be performed by the customer
Required Participants: Technical Lead; Identity Owner; Compliance Owner
Default If Undecided: Request read-only roles and use customer execution for privileged changes
Engineering Notes: Document every role, assignment method, start date and expiration.

Customer Question: Who owns public DNS, and who can approve and implement DNS changes?
Why This Must Be Asked: Email authentication, tenant verification, federation and migration work can be blocked without DNS access.
Expected Answer Type: Named provider, owner and change process
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Customer IT; external web vendor; registrar provider; MSP; parent organization
Configuration Impact: Determines SPF, DKIM, DMARC, MX, Autodiscover and domain-verification implementation paths
Required Participants: DNS Owner; Security Owner; Change Manager
Default If Undecided: Treat DNS changes as customer-executed
Engineering Notes: Collect current TTL values and the provider’s expected change lead time.

Customer Question: Where may project documentation, configuration exports and security evidence be stored?
Why This Must Be Asked: Exports may contain privileged, security-sensitive or personal information.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Dedicated SharePoint site; customer GRC platform; encrypted project repository; customer-only repository
Configuration Impact: Determines evidence storage, membership, sharing, retention and project closeout procedures
Required Participants: Project Manager; Technical Lead; Records Owner
Default If Undecided: Use a customer-controlled restricted SharePoint site
Engineering Notes: Do not place secrets, passwords or unrestricted personal data in the repository.

Customer Question: Which platform is considered authoritative for corporate device inventory?
Why This Must Be Asked: Multiple platforms frequently contain duplicate, stale or incomplete device records.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Intune; NinjaOne; another RMM; Microsoft Defender; CMDB; Active Directory; procurement system
Configuration Impact: Determines device reconciliation, enrollment scope and unmanaged-device identification
Default If Undecided: Use reconciled Intune, Entra, Defender and RMM data
Engineering Notes: The authoritative inventory can still require supporting data from other platforms.

Customer Question: Will personally owned devices be allowed to access organizational data?
Why This Must Be Asked: This decision drives enrollment restrictions, application protection, compliance, Conditional Access, data download and support boundaries.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: No BYOD; mobile BYOD with app protection only; enrolled mobile BYOD; Windows BYOD; browser-only BYOD; limited contractor BYOD
Configuration Impact: Affects GBL-P1-EPS-002, compliance policies, app protection, Conditional Access and unmanaged-device restrictions
Required Participants: Endpoint Owner; HR; Legal; Service Desk; Business Owners
Required By: Before Intune and Conditional Access design
Default If Undecided: Block personal enrollment and allow browser access only through approved restrictions
Engineering Notes: Make the decision separately for Windows, macOS, iOS or iPadOS and Android.

Customer Question: Which device platforms and ownership models will the organization support and manage?
Why This Must Be Asked: Engineers need defined supported platforms before selecting enrollment, compliance and security settings.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Corporate Windows; corporate macOS; corporate iPhone or iPad; Android Enterprise; shared devices; kiosks; virtual desktops
Configuration Impact: Determines enrollment restrictions, platform policies, compliance rules, application deployment and support scope
Required Participants: Security Owner; Service Desk; Business Owners
Default If Undecided: Support corporate Windows and approved mobile application protection only
Engineering Notes: Include minimum supported OS versions and expected hardware lifecycle.

Customer Question: How quickly must unsupported operating systems be upgraded, replaced or isolated?
Why This Must Be Asked: The answer determines compliance minimums, update policy deadlines, exceptions and technical-debt prioritization.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Immediate isolation; 30 days; 60 days; 90 days; next hardware refresh
Configuration Impact: Drives minimum OS compliance settings, update rings and vulnerability exceptions
Default If Undecided: Unsupported systems are noncompliant and require a time-bound exception
Engineering Notes: Identify systems that cannot be upgraded because of application or hardware dependencies.

Customer Question: Who approves applications and maintains the authoritative application catalog?
Why This Must Be Asked: Application deployment, allowlisting and SaaS governance require accountable ownership.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Application Review Board; IT; Security; department owner; procurement
Configuration Impact: Determines application inventory governance, packaging, application control and approval workflow
Default If Undecided: Require business and security approval for managed applications
Engineering Notes: Include owner, publisher, support status, installation source and data sensitivity.

Customer Question: May users install applications, browser extensions or add-ins without IT approval?
Why This Must Be Asked: This affects local administrator policy, application control, browser extension policy and Microsoft 365 add-in settings.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: No user installation; approved catalog only; approved browser extensions; department-managed software; unrestricted with monitoring
Configuration Impact: Drives application allowlisting, local-admin controls, Intune Company Portal and extension restrictions
Required Participants: Endpoint Owner; Application Owner; Business Owners
Default If Undecided: Allow installation only through approved managed catalog
Engineering Notes: Differentiate desktop software, browser extensions, Office add-ins and mobile applications.

Customer Question: Does the customer intend to retain, reduce or retire on-premises Active Directory and server infrastructure?
Why This Must Be Asked: This affects Entra Connect, hybrid join, Group Policy, Windows Hello, application authentication and server remediation.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Remain hybrid; reduce server footprint; transition to cloud-only; undecided
Configuration Impact: Determines identity architecture, device join model, GPO modernization and domain-controller roadmap
Required Participants: Infrastructure Owner; Identity Owner; Application Owners
Default If Undecided: Stabilize hybrid identity first and defer decommissioning
Engineering Notes: Cloud-only should be treated as an outcome requiring dependency removal, not only a licensing decision.

Customer Question: How will the customer handle applications or devices that require legacy protocols, domain authentication or unsupported servers?
Why This Must Be Asked: These dependencies can block security controls and cloud migration.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Replace; upgrade; isolate; accept temporarily; retire; move to vendor-hosted service
Configuration Impact: Drives exceptions for legacy authentication, network access, service accounts, patching and server decommissioning
Required Participants: Security Owner; Business Owner; Executive Sponsor
Default If Undecided: Isolate and create a time-bound remediation plan
Engineering Notes: Each accepted dependency needs an owner, risk approval and retirement date.

Customer Question: What should happen when an unapproved cloud application is discovered?
Why This Must Be Asked: Discovery without an agreed response produces unresolved shadow-IT risk.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Monitor; notify owner; require review; block; migrate data; sanction after assessment
Configuration Impact: Determines Defender for Cloud Apps governance, application risk workflow and network or endpoint blocking
Required Participants: Application Owner; Legal; Procurement; Business Owners
Default If Undecided: Require review and block only high-risk applications after impact validation
Engineering Notes: Do not automatically block during discovery unless there is an active threat.

Customer Question: Which system is authoritative for employee status, manager, department and role?
Why This Must Be Asked: Identity automation and access governance depend on reliable source attributes.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: HR system; Active Directory; Microsoft Entra ID; payroll system; manual IT process
Configuration Impact: Determines joiner-mover-leaver automation, dynamic groups, access reviews and ownership workflows
Default If Undecided: Use HR for personnel status and Entra or Active Directory for technical identity state
Engineering Notes: Document synchronization timing and who corrects bad source data.

Customer Question: After how many days without approved activity should a user account be reviewed, disabled or removed?
Why This Must Be Asked: The threshold determines inactive-account reporting and remediation behavior.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: 30 days; 45 days; 60 days; 90 days; separate employee and guest thresholds
Configuration Impact: Drives GBL-P1-IAM-004 and Phase 4 inactive-account operations
Required Participants: HR; Identity Owner; Legal; Service Desk
Default If Undecided: Review at 45 days and disable after owner validation
Engineering Notes: Define exceptions for leave, seasonal workers, service accounts and emergency accounts.

Customer Question: How long should guest access remain active before expiration or mandatory review?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines access-package expiration, guest reviews and collaboration lifecycle.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: 30 days; 90 days; 180 days; one year; contract end date
Configuration Impact: Drives guest expiration, sponsor reviews and external collaboration settings
Default If Undecided: 90-day review with maximum one-year access unless renewed
Engineering Notes: Partner, vendor and one-time guest populations may need different durations.

Customer Question: Will service accounts be retained, migrated to managed identities or replaced with workload identities?
Why This Must Be Asked: Service accounts affect authentication, password rotation, Conditional Access exclusions and privileged access.
Expected Answer Type: Decision per service account or application
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Managed identity; workload identity; group managed service account; certificate; retained password account; retire
Configuration Impact: Determines service-account remediation and authentication design
Required Participants: Security Owner; Infrastructure Owner; Application Vendor
Default If Undecided: Retain temporarily with owner, strong credential control and migration plan
Engineering Notes: Do not disable interactive access until the application dependency is validated.

Customer Question: Will administrators use separate privileged and standard productivity accounts?
Why This Must Be Asked: This drives account creation, licensing, Conditional Access and privileged workstation requirements.
Expected Answer Type: Yes or No plus affected roles
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Separate accounts for all administrators; separate accounts only for high-impact roles; combined accounts with compensating controls
Configuration Impact: Drives privileged-account separation and phishing-resistant MFA scope
Default If Undecided: Use separate privileged accounts for high-impact roles
Engineering Notes: Document the productivity-license approach for administrative accounts.

Customer Question: Will privileged roles be permanent, eligible through PIM, or assigned through role-assignable groups?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines role assignment type, approval, activation duration and licensing requirements.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: PIM eligible; permanent active; group eligible; emergency only
Configuration Impact: Drives PIM configuration and privileged-access reviews
Required Participants: Identity Owner; IT Leadership; Licensing Owner
Default If Undecided: Use PIM-eligible assignments for supported human administrator roles
Engineering Notes: Permanent access requires explicit operational justification.

Customer Question: Who will hold emergency credentials, and how will emergency use be approved and monitored?
Why This Must Be Asked: Engineers cannot safely configure break-glass accounts without custody and response decisions.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Security executive; CIO; two-person vault access; managed password vault; sealed offline credential
Configuration Impact: Determines emergency-account configuration, monitoring, testing and credential rotation
Default If Undecided: Maintain two cloud-only accounts with separate secure custodians and alert on all use
Engineering Notes: Do not perform production sign-in tests without an approved change.

Customer Question: Which Microsoft license level is approved for the target state?
Why This Must Be Asked: Conditional Access risk policies, PIM, Endpoint DLP, advanced eDiscovery and other settings depend on licensing.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Business Premium; Microsoft 365 E3; Microsoft 365 E5; E5 Security; E5 Compliance; Entra Suite; individual add-ons
Configuration Impact: Determines which baseline settings are available, blocked by license or require alternate controls
Required Participants: Technical Lead; Security Owner; Compliance Owner; Finance
Default If Undecided: Design to currently owned licenses and identify optional premium controls separately
Engineering Notes: Do not treat trial features as approved production licensing.

Customer Question: What level of residual risk will leadership accept, and who can formally approve exceptions?
Why This Must Be Asked: Engineering needs an approval boundary when the full baseline cannot be implemented.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: No high risk accepted; high risk requires executive approval; medium risk requires security approval; low risk accepted by control owner
Configuration Impact: Drives exception workflow, roadmap priorities and Phase 4 governance
Default If Undecided: High and critical risks require executive approval
Engineering Notes: Include exception duration and required compensating controls.

Customer Question: Which authentication methods will be permitted for standard users, privileged users, contractors and guests?
Why This Must Be Asked: The answer determines Authentication Methods policy, authentication strengths and migration planning.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Authenticator push; passwordless Authenticator; FIDO2 or passkey; certificate authentication; SMS; voice; Temporary Access Pass
Configuration Impact: Drives MFA, passwordless, recovery and Conditional Access settings
Required Participants: Identity Owner; Service Desk; Accessibility or HR representatives
Default If Undecided: Authenticator for standard users and phishing-resistant methods for privileged users
Engineering Notes: Accessibility and unsupported-device exceptions need documented alternatives.

Customer Question: Should MFA enforcement occur tenant-wide, by department, by application, or by risk group?
Why This Must Be Asked: Rollout strategy affects user impact, support volume, pilot design and enforcement timing.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Privileged users first; pilot department; all users by location; application-by-application; risk-based priority
Configuration Impact: Determines registration campaign, pilot groups and Conditional Access rollout
Required Participants: Identity Owner; Change Manager; Service Desk; Business Leaders
Default If Undecided: Privileged users first, followed by representative pilot and staged production waves
Engineering Notes: Include third-party MFA retirement dependencies.

Customer Question: From which countries or regions should users be permitted to sign in?
Why This Must Be Asked: This drives named locations and country-based Conditional Access policies.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Allow operating countries; block all others; monitor only; no country restriction
Configuration Impact: Determines location controls and travel exception workflow
Required Participants: HR; Legal; Business Leaders; Service Desk
Default If Undecided: Monitor first and block only countries with no legitimate business use
Engineering Notes: Country controls are supplemental because VPNs and proxies can alter apparent location.

Customer Question: Should corporate public IP addresses be marked as trusted, and should trust change any authentication requirement?
Why This Must Be Asked: Trusted locations can reduce or bypass controls if used too broadly.
Expected Answer Type: Yes or No plus intended effect
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Document only; trusted for risk context; MFA bypass for limited legacy scenario; no trusted locations
Configuration Impact: Determines named locations and CA conditions
Default If Undecided: Document corporate IPs but do not bypass MFA based only on location
Engineering Notes: Verify static ownership and recurring IP review.

Customer Question: How frequently should users and administrators be required to reauthenticate?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines sign-in frequency and persistent-browser session settings.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Every time for sensitive action; 4 hours; 8 hours; 24 hours; 7 days; application default
Required Participants: Identity Owner; Business Owners; Service Desk
Default If Undecided: Use service defaults for ordinary users and stricter controls for administrators and sensitive applications
Engineering Notes: Avoid prompt frequency that encourages unsafe MFA approval behavior.

Customer Question: Which users and applications must require a compliant or managed device?
Why This Must Be Asked: A broad managed-device requirement can block BYOD, contractors and unsupported platforms.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Administrators; all employees; finance and HR; Azure management; SharePoint; Exchange; sensitive applications
Configuration Impact: Determines device-compliance Conditional Access scope and exception paths
Required Participants: Endpoint Owner; Application Owners; Business Leaders
Required By: Before Conditional Access and Intune enforcement
Default If Undecided: Require compliant devices for administrators and sensitive applications; use app protection or browser restrictions elsewhere
Engineering Notes: Validate at least one compliant device per supported platform before enforcement.

Customer Question: Which repositories should be considered authoritative for business information?
Why This Must Be Asked: This drives information architecture, migration, search, Copilot grounding and agent data-source approval.
Expected Answer Type: Repository list with owner and data domain
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: SharePoint sites; Teams-connected sites; file shares; SQL systems; Dataverse; Fabric; line-of-business systems
Configuration Impact: Determines migration priority, information architecture and AI grounding scope
Required Participants: Technical Lead; Data Governance Owner; Application Owners
Default If Undecided: Treat no repository as authoritative until a data owner approves it
Engineering Notes: Authority requires ownership, accuracy and maintenance, not just current usage.

Customer Question: Should existing file shares or third-party storage be migrated, restructured, archived or retained?
Why This Must Be Asked: This determines migration tooling, SharePoint architecture, permission remediation and AI readiness.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Migrate to SharePoint; migrate to Azure Files; retain; archive; delete stale content; hybrid approach
Configuration Impact: Determines data-modernization roadmap and target repository design
Required Participants: Technical Lead; Infrastructure Owner; Department Owners
Default If Undecided: Assess and design before selecting target platform
Engineering Notes: Avoid direct one-to-one migration of poor folder structures without owner review.

Customer Question: Will users be allowed to share files and sites with external people?
Why This Must Be Asked: This controls tenant sharing maximums, site settings, guest governance and anonymous-link policies.
Expected Answer Type: Single choice plus approved use cases
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: No external sharing; guests only; new and existing guests; Anyone links for approved sites; partner domains only
Configuration Impact: Drives SharePoint, OneDrive, Teams and Entra external-collaboration controls
Default If Undecided: Allow authenticated guests only and disable Anyone links by default
Engineering Notes: Identify business units that require client, vendor or partner collaboration.

Customer Question: If Anyone links are permitted, how long should they remain active?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines SharePoint and OneDrive link-expiration settings.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: 1 day; 7 days; 14 days; 30 days; other approved period
Configuration Impact: Drives anonymous-link expiration and recurring exposure monitoring
Default If Undecided: Disable Anyone links; where approved, expire within 14 days
Engineering Notes: The maximum expiration can differ from the safer user default.

Customer Question: Should external sharing use an allowlist, blocklist, or unrestricted domain model?
Why This Must Be Asked: Incorrect domain restrictions can either expose information or disrupt legitimate collaboration.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Approved-domain allowlist; prohibited-domain blocklist; no domain restrictions; site-specific restrictions
Configuration Impact: Determines SharePoint, Teams and Entra domain controls
Default If Undecided: Use no allowlist unless the customer can maintain it; block known prohibited domains where justified
Engineering Notes: Assign ownership for keeping the list current.

Customer Question: Is organization-wide access acceptable for any repositories, and who can approve it?
Why This Must Be Asked: Engineers need to distinguish legitimate publishing sites from accidental oversharing.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Prohibit broad access; allow approved intranet publishing; allow organization-wide knowledge sites; require annual certification
Configuration Impact: Determines permission-remediation thresholds and AI readiness gates
Default If Undecided: Prohibit broad access to sensitive repositories and require owner approval elsewhere
Engineering Notes: Everyone-style access should be treated as intentional only when documented.

Customer Question: Should direct user permissions be permitted, or should access be provided only through managed groups?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines permission architecture and remediation design.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Groups only; direct permissions allowed for confidential cases; direct permissions allowed temporarily; current model retained
Configuration Impact: Drives SharePoint and Teams permission remediation
Default If Undecided: Use managed groups and permit direct access only through documented exceptions
Engineering Notes: Extensive unique permissions may justify separate sites or libraries.

Customer Question: What information-classification levels does the customer require?
Why This Must Be Asked: Sensitivity labels and handling controls cannot be designed until the business taxonomy is approved.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Public; Internal; Confidential; Highly Confidential; regulated sublabels
Configuration Impact: Determines sensitivity-label taxonomy, encryption and DLP conditions
Required Participants: Legal; Security; Data Owners; Executive Sponsor
Default If Undecided: Use a simple four-level model pending customer approval
Engineering Notes: Each level should produce a meaningful difference in handling.

Customer Question: Should users be required to label documents and email?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines publishing-policy behavior and user impact.
Expected Answer Type: Yes or No by workload and user group
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Mandatory for documents; mandatory for email; mandatory for selected users; default label only; optional
Required Participants: Security Owner; Legal; Business Owners; Change Manager
Default If Undecided: Pilot a default nonrestrictive label before mandatory labeling
Engineering Notes: Mandatory labeling requires training and compatibility testing.

Customer Question: Which classifications require encryption, and who should retain access?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines label encryption, external sharing and recovery configuration.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Internal users; named users; approved groups; partner domains; user-defined permissions; no encryption
Configuration Impact: Drives label-based encryption and rights-management controls
Default If Undecided: Encrypt only the highest approved classification during pilot
Engineering Notes: Test service accounts, external recipients, search, eDiscovery and recovery.

Customer Question: Should DLP warn, require justification, block, or monitor each sensitive-data scenario?
Why This Must Be Asked: Engineers need a business-approved action model before enforcing policies.
Expected Answer Type: Matrix by data type, destination and severity
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Audit only; warn; allow override with justification; block with override; block without override
Configuration Impact: Determines DLP rules, policy tips, override behavior and incident severity
Required Participants: Data Owners; Legal; Service Desk; Business Owners
Default If Undecided: Start in simulation and use warnings before blocking unless risk requires otherwise
Engineering Notes: High-risk data and unauthorized external destinations can use stricter actions.

Customer Question: Who should receive and investigate DLP alerts?
Why This Must Be Asked: Alerts can expose sensitive content and require accountable, trained recipients.
Expected Answer Type: Named role or queue by severity
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Security Operations; Compliance; Data Owner; Privacy; Service Desk; dedicated DLP analysts
Configuration Impact: Determines alert routing, role assignments and investigation workflow
Required Participants: Privacy; Legal; Data Governance; Service Manager
Default If Undecided: Route alerts to a restricted security or compliance queue
Engineering Notes: Do not send sensitive incident data to broad distribution groups.

Customer Question: How long must email, files, Teams messages, AI interactions and business records be retained?
Why This Must Be Asked: Retention settings require legal and business decisions and must not be chosen solely by engineers.
Expected Answer Type: Duration and trigger by data category
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: One year; three years; seven years; employment plus period; contract expiration plus period; permanent
Configuration Impact: Drives retention policies, retention labels, event-based retention and storage impact
Required Participants: Compliance; Data Owners; HR; Finance; Security
Default If Undecided: Do not configure destructive retention until legal requirements are approved
Engineering Notes: Ask separately about retain-only, delete-after, records and legal-hold requirements.

Customer Question: Should content be deleted automatically at retention expiration or reviewed before deletion?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines records-management labels and disposition-review workflows.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Automatic deletion; one-stage review; multistage review; permanent retention
Configuration Impact: Drives disposition settings, reviewers and operational workload
Default If Undecided: Require review for regulated and high-value records; use automatic deletion only when explicitly approved
Engineering Notes: Identify backup or recovery expectations separately from retention.

Customer Question: Which AI services are approved, restricted or prohibited for organizational use?
Why This Must Be Asked: The answer determines application controls, DLP scope, agent governance and user communications.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Microsoft 365 Copilot; Copilot Chat; Copilot Studio; Azure OpenAI; third-party AI; consumer Copilot; developer AI tools
Configuration Impact: Determines AI application inventory, access, monitoring and acceptable-use controls
Customer Decision Owner: Executive Sponsor or AI Governance Owner
Required Participants: Security; Legal; Privacy; Data Governance; Development Leaders
Required By: Before AI architecture and policy design
Default If Undecided: Permit only approved enterprise AI services and restrict organizational data in unapproved services
Engineering Notes: Include browser extensions, SaaS-embedded AI and developer tools.

Customer Question: Who should receive Microsoft 365 Copilot first, and what repositories should be in scope?
Why This Must Be Asked: This determines pilot users, license assignment, data remediation priority and validation personas.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Executives; IT; sales; HR; finance; pilot champions; selected departments
Configuration Impact: Drives Copilot pilot group, AI readiness remediation and access validation
Customer Decision Owner: Executive Sponsor or AI Governance Owner
Required Participants: Department Leaders; Security; Data Owners; Licensing Owner
Default If Undecided: Use a small representative pilot and exclude high-risk repositories until validated
Engineering Notes: Choose users who will provide useful feedback without giving the pilot unnecessary access.

Customer Question: Who may create, publish and share Copilot agents?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines maker permissions, environment design, approval workflow and agent inventory scope.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: IT only; approved makers; department makers; all licensed users; development environment only
Configuration Impact: Drives agent governance, Power Platform environment controls and publication approval
Required Participants: Power Platform Owner; Security; Data Governance; Business Leaders
Default If Undecided: Restrict production publication to approved makers and allow development in governed environments
Engineering Notes: Creation, publication and tenant-wide sharing should be treated as separate permissions.

Customer Question: Which connectors and external data sources may agents use?
Why This Must Be Asked: Connectors can extend an agent beyond Microsoft 365 permissions and permit external actions or data movement.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Microsoft 365 read-only; Dataverse; SQL; custom APIs; third-party SaaS; write-enabled connectors; prohibited connectors
Configuration Impact: Drives data policies, connector allowlists, security review and agent risk tier
Required Participants: Application Owners; Data Owners; Power Platform Administrator
Default If Undecided: Allow approved Microsoft 365 read-only connectors in development and require review for all others
Engineering Notes: Evaluate authentication, delegated permissions, data destinations and write or delete capability.

Customer Question: What is the desired target state and by what date must it be achieved?
Why This Must Be Asked: Architecture may require interim states if licenses, applications, hardware or business readiness are not available immediately.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Hybrid stabilization; cloud-only identity; fully managed endpoints; modernized data; Copilot-ready governance
Configuration Impact: Determines interim architecture, project waves and resource plan
Default If Undecided: Use phased stabilization, modernization and governance sequence
Engineering Notes: Separate aspirational end state from the funded implementation scope.

Customer Question: How should each identified gap be treated?
Why This Must Be Asked: Engineers need consistent dispositions to convert findings into actionable work.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Remediate; accept; transfer; defer; blocked by license; blocked by dependency; not applicable
Configuration Impact: Populates risk register, backlog, exception register and roadmap
Default If Undecided: Mark unresolved items as remediation required
Engineering Notes: Do not use not applicable when the control is merely inconvenient or unlicensed.

Customer Question: Which risk method and thresholds should be used to prioritize findings?
Why This Must Be Asked: Consistent scoring is required to compare identity, devices, data, applications and AI risks.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Customer risk matrix; likelihood-impact matrix; regulatory severity; cyber-insurance controls; combined method
Configuration Impact: Determines roadmap priority and escalation thresholds
Default If Undecided: Use likelihood and business-impact scoring with critical, high, medium and low categories
Engineering Notes: Document inherent risk, compensating controls and residual risk separately.

Customer Question: Which areas should be remediated first when resource or budget constraints prevent simultaneous implementation?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines sequencing and resource allocation across security, migration, data and AI work.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Identity; MFA; Conditional Access; endpoints; email; data migration; Purview; Copilot; agents
Configuration Impact: Drives project waves and staffing plan
Required Participants: Security Owner; Technical Lead; Business Leaders
Default If Undecided: Prioritize identity, emergency access, MFA, Conditional Access and endpoint visibility before broad migration or AI rollout
Engineering Notes: Dependencies may override stated preference when foundational controls are missing.

Customer Question: When may engineers implement user-impacting or service-impacting changes?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines elapsed duration, staffing, communications and rollback planning.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Business hours; evenings; weekends; maintenance windows; fiscal close blackout; seasonal blackout
Configuration Impact: Drives project plan and change scheduling
Required Participants: Business Owners; Service Desk; Executive Sponsor
Default If Undecided: Use approved after-hours maintenance windows for high-impact changes
Engineering Notes: Include time-zone, notice and emergency-change requirements.

Customer Question: Who approves changes to identity, Conditional Access, endpoint, email, Purview and AI settings?
Why This Must Be Asked: Different control families may require different decision owners.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Security approves CA; endpoint owner approves Intune; legal approves retention; data owner approves repository access; AI board approves agents
Configuration Impact: Determines change workflow and baseline ownership
Required Participants: Workstream Owners; Change Manager; Compliance Owner
Default If Undecided: Require Technical Lead and Security Owner approval, plus business or legal owner where applicable
Engineering Notes: Engineering implementation authority does not equal business risk acceptance.

Customer Question: How frequently does the customer want project, security, risk and executive reporting?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines report generation, meeting schedule and escalation timing.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Weekly project status; monthly service review; quarterly executive review; immediate critical-risk escalation
Configuration Impact: Drives governance meetings and reporting workload
Required Participants: Executive Sponsor; Service Manager; Security Owner
Default If Undecided: Weekly project status and monthly leadership summary
Engineering Notes: Define who receives each report and which information is confidential.

Customer Question: Which change-management process must engineers follow?
Why This Must Be Asked: Implementation cannot begin safely without approval, validation and rollback requirements.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Customer CAB; MSP change process; joint approval; emergency change; standard preapproved change
Configuration Impact: Determines ticketing, evidence, implementation timing and rollback
Required Participants: Technical Lead; Service Manager; Security Owner
Default If Undecided: Require documented change, validation and rollback for all material production changes
Engineering Notes: Identify standard changes that may be preapproved.

Customer Question: Who writes, approves and sends user-impacting communications?
Why This Must Be Asked: MFA, device enrollment, labeling, DLP and migration projects can fail without coordinated communication.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Customer communications; HR; IT; department leaders; MSP drafts and customer sends
Configuration Impact: Determines communication deliverables and project dependencies
Required Participants: HR; Service Desk; Executive Sponsor; Department Leaders
Default If Undecided: MSP drafts and customer approves and sends
Engineering Notes: Include minimum notice requirements and emergency communication procedure.

Customer Question: Which users require training, what format is required, and how will completion be tracked?
Why This Must Be Asked: User-facing controls require different training for users, owners, administrators and support personnel.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Live sessions; recorded training; knowledge articles; office hours; role-based workshops; tracked LMS completion
Configuration Impact: Determines adoption plan and phase acceptance
Required Participants: HR; Service Desk; Data Owners; Compliance; AI Governance Owner
Default If Undecided: Provide role-based knowledge articles and pilot training
Engineering Notes: Separate end-user, data-owner, administrator, investigator and agent-maker training.

Customer Question: Which system or team authorizes account creation, role changes and account termination?
Why This Must Be Asked: Engineers need an authoritative trigger before automating identity lifecycle actions.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: HR system; payroll system; Active Directory; Microsoft Entra ID; IT ticket; manager approval
Configuration Impact: Determines identity automation, approval workflow, source attributes and audit evidence
Required Participants: HR; Identity Operations; Security; Service Desk
Default If Undecided: Use HR as the personnel authority and ITSM as the technical fulfillment record
Engineering Notes: Document how contractors, vendors and nonemployee identities are handled.

Customer Question: How far in advance should new accounts be created, and when may they become active?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines provisioning timing and reduces unused active-account exposure.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Create one business day before start; create seven days before but block sign-in; activate on start date
Configuration Impact: Determines account-enabled state, license assignment and onboarding automation
Default If Undecided: Create in advance but block sign-in until the approved start date
Engineering Notes: Licenses and group memberships may also need delayed activation.

Customer Question: What access should every employee receive automatically, and what requires separate approval?
Why This Must Be Asked: Defines the minimum access profile and prevents excessive default permissions.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Microsoft 365 license; baseline groups; Teams; department groups; business applications
Configuration Impact: Determines group-based licensing, dynamic groups and application assignments
Required Participants: HR; Department Owners; Application Owners; Security
Default If Undecided: Assign only baseline productivity access and require approval for departmental or sensitive access
Engineering Notes: Separate employee, contractor, intern and vendor profiles.

Customer Question: May employees temporarily retain old access after changing departments or job functions?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines whether old access is removed immediately or retained during a transition.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: No overlap; 7 days; 14 days; manager-approved period
Configuration Impact: Determines mover workflow, access expiration and review requirements
Required Participants: HR; Current Manager; New Manager; Data Owners
Default If Undecided: Remove old access immediately unless a time-bound exception is approved
Engineering Notes: Privileged and sensitive-data access should normally be removed immediately.

Customer Question: How quickly after termination notice must access be disabled and sessions revoked?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines the urgency and automation of the leaver process.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Immediate for involuntary; end of final workday for voluntary; scheduled future disablement
Configuration Impact: Determines account disablement, session revocation and escalation workflow
Required Participants: HR; Legal; Identity Operations; Service Desk
Default If Undecided: Immediate for involuntary terminations and at the approved end time for planned departures
Engineering Notes: Use exact timestamps and time zones for scheduled departures.

Customer Question: What should happen to a departed user's mailbox, OneDrive, files, Teams ownership and application data?
Why This Must Be Asked: Account disablement alone does not address business data continuity or retention.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Convert mailbox; grant delegate access; transfer OneDrive; retain for defined period; delete after retention
Configuration Impact: Determines license retention, mailbox conversion, OneDrive transfer and data-owner assignments
Required Participants: HR; Legal; Manager; Messaging Owner; Collaboration Owner
Default If Undecided: Disable access, transfer ownership, preserve required data and remove unnecessary licenses after validation
Engineering Notes: Legal holds and retention requirements override ordinary deletion.

Customer Question: After how many days without approved activity should an employee account be reviewed and disabled?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines the inactivity report and remediation schedule.
Configuration Impact: Configures reporting thresholds, owner notification and disable workflow
Default If Undecided: Review at 45 days and disable after owner validation
Engineering Notes: Use interactive and noninteractive activity and account type.

Customer Question: How long should disabled accounts remain before deletion?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines account cleanup, recovery window and identity-retention requirements.
Expected Answer Type: Number of days by account type
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: 30; 90; 180; 365 days; never automatically delete
Configuration Impact: Determines deletion automation and license-removal timing
Default If Undecided: Retain disabled accounts for 90 days while removing unnecessary licenses after data review
Engineering Notes: Account deletion must be coordinated with mailbox, OneDrive and legal requirements.

Customer Question: Who may invite external users into the tenant?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines Entra external-collaboration settings and guest-request workflow.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Administrators only; Guest Inviter group; site owners; all employees; approved request workflow
Configuration Impact: Configures invitation restrictions, Guest Inviter assignments and provisioning workflow
Default If Undecided: Allow only an approved Guest Inviter group or request workflow
Engineering Notes: A restrictive setting requires a responsive guest-request process.

Customer Question: How long may guest access remain active before expiration or renewal?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines guest expiration and recurring access-review frequency.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: 30; 90; 180; 365 days; contract end date
Configuration Impact: Configures access-package duration, review cadence and expiration
Default If Undecided: Require 90-day review and expire no later than one year unless renewed
Engineering Notes: Vendors, clients and one-time guests can use different durations.

Customer Question: Who must sponsor guests, and what must the sponsor certify?
Why This Must Be Asked: Guest access requires accountable business ownership.
Expected Answer Type: Named sponsor role and certification items
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Requesting employee; department manager; site owner; vendor manager
Configuration Impact: Determines guest metadata, review assignments and renewal decisions
Default If Undecided: Require an internal employee sponsor to certify purpose, resources and duration
Engineering Notes: Define reassignment when a sponsor leaves.

Customer Question: Which service accounts, if any, require interactive sign-in?
Why This Must Be Asked: Blocking interactive sign-in can break applications if dependencies are unknown.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: No interactive sign-in; approved administrative service login; temporary migration exception
Configuration Impact: Determines Conditional Access blocking, account restrictions and exception scope
Default If Undecided: Block interactive sign-in unless a documented dependency is validated
Engineering Notes: Every retained exception needs an owner and retirement date.

Customer Question: What credential type and rotation period should service identities use?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines whether accounts use passwords, certificates, managed identities or federated credentials.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Managed identity; gMSA; certificate; federated identity; password rotated every 30 or 90 days
Configuration Impact: Determines workload-identity migration and credential-management settings
Default If Undecided: Prefer managed or workload identities; otherwise use rotated strong credentials
Engineering Notes: Avoid nonexpiring client secrets and passwords.

Customer Question: Which company names, brands, locations, product names and predictable terms must be blocked in passwords?
Why This Must Be Asked: Customer-specific terms are required for an effective custom banned-password list.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Company name; abbreviations; product names; local sports teams; office locations
Configuration Impact: Configures Microsoft Entra custom banned-password list
Default If Undecided: Block company names and common brand variations
Engineering Notes: Do not include actual user passwords in the list or evidence.

Customer Question: What failed-attempt threshold and lockout duration will be used?
Why This Must Be Asked: Overly aggressive settings can cause denial of service, while weak values reduce protection.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Microsoft defaults; 10 attempts and 60 seconds; customer-defined values
Default If Undecided: Use Microsoft-recommended defaults unless evidence supports a change
Engineering Notes: Review application behavior and help-desk impact before using lower thresholds.

Customer Question: Which MFA methods are approved for employees, administrators, guests and contractors?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines Authentication Methods policy and authentication strengths.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Authenticator push; passkeys or FIDO2; certificate authentication; SMS; voice; software OATH; Temporary Access Pass
Configuration Impact: Configures method enablement and user-group scope
Required Participants: Identity Owner; HR; Accessibility; Service Desk
Default If Undecided: Authenticator for standard users and phishing-resistant methods for privileged users
Engineering Notes: Provide an approved accessibility and account-recovery alternative.

Customer Question: Should SMS and voice remain available, and for which users?
Why This Must Be Asked: Removing weak methods without an alternative can lock users out.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Disable immediately; retain temporarily for selected users; retain as recovery only; retain indefinitely by exception
Configuration Impact: Determines SMS and voice method scope and migration campaign
Default If Undecided: Disable for privileged users and migrate standard users through staged rollout
Engineering Notes: Every long-term exception requires a documented risk decision.

Customer Question: Who may issue Temporary Access Passes, for what purposes, and with what lifetime?
Why This Must Be Asked: TAP can bootstrap strong authentication and must be tightly governed.
Expected Answer Type: Role, purpose, lifetime and use count
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Help desk after identity verification; 1 hour; 8 hours; one-time use; reusable during device setup
Configuration Impact: Configures TAP policy, help-desk roles and issuance procedure
Default If Undecided: Allow authorized help desk issuance for onboarding and recovery with short lifetime and one-time use
Engineering Notes: Define identity-verification evidence before issuance.

Customer Question: Should Authenticator push, number matching, application context, location context and passwordless phone sign-in be enabled?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines the exact Microsoft Authenticator method configuration.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Push enabled; number matching required; application context enabled; location context enabled; passwordless pilot only
Required Participants: Identity Owner; Service Desk; Privacy Owner
Default If Undecided: Enable push, number matching and context; pilot passwordless phone sign-in
Engineering Notes: Geographic context is informational and may be inaccurate.

Customer Question: How long should users have to complete combined MFA and SSPR registration?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines campaign timing, enforcement date and support workload.
Expected Answer Type: Number of days and escalation schedule
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: 7; 14; 30 days with reminders
Configuration Impact: Configures registration campaign and communication plan
Required Participants: Change Manager; Service Desk; Department Leaders
Default If Undecided: Provide 14 days with reminders and manager escalation
Engineering Notes: Complete registration before the related Conditional Access enforcement wave.

Customer Question: Which groups should receive the registration campaign first?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines pilot and production rollout sequence.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: IT first; administrators first; pilot department; all employees; contractors last
Required Participants: Change Manager; Department Leaders; Service Desk
Default If Undecided: IT and representative pilot users first, followed by staged production groups
Engineering Notes: Exclude service and emergency accounts.

Customer Question: Which users and applications must require phishing-resistant authentication?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines where FIDO2, passkeys or certificate authentication is mandatory.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Global Administrators; all administrators; finance executives; Azure management; security portals; privileged workstations
Configuration Impact: Configures authentication strengths and Conditional Access scope
Required Participants: Identity Owner; Application Owners; Executive Sponsor
Default If Undecided: Require phishing-resistant authentication for high-impact administrative roles
Engineering Notes: Confirm method registration before enforcement.

Customer Question: Which applications and user groups still depend on per-user MFA, Duo, Okta or another provider?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines migration waves, coexistence and decommission timing.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Migrate; retain temporarily; replace application; retire
Configuration Impact: Determines legacy MFA exceptions and decommission plan
Default If Undecided: Retain temporarily with time-bound migration plan
Engineering Notes: Do not remove the legacy provider until sign-in validation is complete.

Customer Question: Who may use self-service password reset?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines SSPR assignment and support model.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: All employees; cloud-only users; synchronized users; pilot group; no contractors
Default If Undecided: Pilot employees and expand after validation
Engineering Notes: Privileged and emergency accounts may need a separate recovery procedure.

Customer Question: Which methods and how many methods should SSPR require?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines reset security and user experience.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Authenticator plus FIDO2; two methods; mobile app only; SMS by exception
Configuration Impact: Configures SSPR authentication methods and registration
Default If Undecided: Require two registered methods and prioritize Authenticator or strong methods
Engineering Notes: Avoid using easily compromised recovery combinations.

Customer Question: Should cloud password resets write back to on-premises Active Directory?
Why This Must Be Asked: Synchronized users may otherwise be unable to reset their authoritative password through Entra.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Enable for all synchronized users; pilot only; not required; blocked by architecture
Configuration Impact: Configures Entra Connect or Cloud Sync writeback
Required By: Before SSPR deployment to synchronized users
Default If Undecided: Enable only after pilot validation and directory health review
Engineering Notes: Confirm permissions, connectivity and on-premises password policy.

Customer Question: Who approves and periodically certifies each administrative role?
Why This Must Be Asked: PIM and access reviews require accountable reviewers.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: CIO; Security Manager; Identity Owner; workload owner
Default If Undecided: Security Owner reviews high-impact roles and workload owners review service roles
Engineering Notes: Reviewers should not approve their own access where avoidable.

Customer Question: Which administrators must receive separate privileged accounts?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines account provisioning, licensing and Conditional Access scope.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: All admins; only high-impact roles; tenant admins; Azure owners; security admins
Configuration Impact: Configures separate accounts and administrative access policies
Required Participants: Identity Owner; IT Leadership; Licensing Owner
Default If Undecided: Use separate accounts for high-impact roles
Engineering Notes: Avoid assigning normal productivity applications to privileged accounts.

Customer Question: Which roles may remain permanently active, and which must be PIM eligible?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines PIM assignment type and operational availability.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: PIM eligible; permanent active; group-based eligible; emergency only
Configuration Impact: Configures active and eligible role assignments
Required Participants: Identity Owner; Workload Owners; Service Manager
Default If Undecided: Human high-impact roles are PIM eligible; service identities use separately governed assignments
Engineering Notes: Permanent active assignments require explicit operational justification.

Customer Question: What authentication, justification, ticket, approval and activation-duration requirements should apply to each role?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines exact PIM role settings.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Phishing-resistant MFA; justification; ticket number; manager approval; 1-hour, 4-hour or 8-hour activation
Required Participants: Identity Owner; Change Manager; Workload Owners
Default If Undecided: Require MFA, justification and ticket; require approval and shorter duration for high-impact roles
Engineering Notes: Assign multiple approvers to maintain availability.

Customer Question: Who may approve activation of Global Administrator, Privileged Role Administrator and other sensitive roles?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines approval workflow and operational coverage.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Security leadership; CIO; identity team leads; on-call approvers
Required Participants: Executive Sponsor; Identity Owner; Service Manager
Default If Undecided: Use at least two qualified approvers and prohibit self-approval
Engineering Notes: Confirm after-hours approval expectations.

Customer Question: Where will emergency-account credentials be stored, and who may retrieve them?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines credential security, two-person control and operational procedure.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Privileged password vault; physical safe; dual custody; executive custody
Default If Undecided: Use two separately protected accounts with separate authorized custodians
Engineering Notes: The vault must remain accessible during an identity or Microsoft cloud outage.

Customer Question: How frequently should active and eligible privileged-role assignments be reviewed?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines access-review recurrence and escalation.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Monthly for Global Administrator; quarterly for other roles; semiannual for low-impact roles
Default If Undecided: Quarterly for all privileged roles and monthly review of highest-impact standing assignments
Engineering Notes: Review permanent and eligible assignments.

Customer Question: How should Conditional Access policies be piloted and rolled out?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines pilot groups, report-only duration, enforcement waves and rollback.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Report-only for 14 days; IT pilot; department waves; all users after acceptance
Configuration Impact: Configures policy state and group assignments
Required Participants: Identity Owner; Change Manager; Service Desk
Default If Undecided: Report-only, engineering pilot, representative business pilot, staged enforcement
Engineering Notes: Emergency corrective policies may use expedited change approval.

Customer Question: Which accounts must be excluded from Conditional Access, and why?
Why This Must Be Asked: Prevents tenant lockout while avoiding unmanaged exclusion sprawl.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Two cloud-only emergency accounts only; approved synchronization account if required
Default If Undecided: Exclude only the approved emergency-access accounts
Engineering Notes: Service accounts should be handled by workload identity design rather than broad user exclusions where possible.

Customer Question: Which accounts, protocols or applications still require legacy authentication?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines scoped exclusions and remediation timeline before blocking.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: SMTP AUTH device; older Office client; scanner; legacy mail application
Default If Undecided: Block legacy authentication except for documented temporary dependencies
Engineering Notes: Every exception needs traffic validation and a target retirement date.

Customer Question: Which roles should be targeted by the privileged-user Conditional Access policy?
Why This Must Be Asked: Different roles may have different security and availability requirements.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: All directory roles; high-impact roles only; Azure owners; Intune and security administrators
Configuration Impact: Configures role targeting for phishing-resistant MFA and session controls
Default If Undecided: Protect all high-impact directory and Azure administrative roles
Engineering Notes: Include privileged role groups and administrative accounts.

Customer Question: Should MFA apply to all cloud applications or only selected applications during rollout?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines application targeting and potential gaps.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: All cloud apps; Microsoft 365 first; Azure management first; selected business apps
Configuration Impact: Configures MFA Conditional Access policy targets
Required Participants: Identity Owner; Application Owners; Service Desk
Default If Undecided: Target all cloud applications after staged validation
Engineering Notes: Avoid long-term fragmented MFA policies that leave uncovered applications.

Customer Question: Should MFA claims from partner tenants be trusted for B2B guests?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines whether guests perform MFA in their home tenant or the resource tenant.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Trust MFA only; trust MFA and device claims; do not trust external claims
Configuration Impact: Configures cross-tenant access settings and guest MFA behavior
Default If Undecided: Trust external MFA only for formally reviewed partner tenants
Engineering Notes: Review partner security requirements before trusting device compliance claims.

Customer Question: Which applications require a compliant device?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines the exact target resources of device-based Conditional Access.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: All Microsoft 365; administrative portals; HR; finance; SharePoint; Exchange; selected sensitive apps
Required Participants: Endpoint Owner; Application Owners; Business Leaders
Default If Undecided: Require compliant devices for administrators and sensitive applications first
Engineering Notes: Coordinate with BYOD and contractor access decisions.

Customer Question: Should noncompliant devices be blocked immediately or receive a remediation grace period?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines user impact and support process.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Immediate block; 24 hours; 3 days; 7 days before block
Configuration Impact: Configures Intune noncompliance actions and Conditional Access timing
Default If Undecided: Use a short grace period for ordinary failures but immediately block high-risk devices
Engineering Notes: Defender high-risk devices can require immediate blocking.

Customer Question: What should happen at low, medium and high user or sign-in risk?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines risk-based policy thresholds and support actions.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Monitor low; require MFA at medium; secure password change at medium user risk; block high
Required Participants: Identity Operations; Security Operations; Service Desk
Default If Undecided: Monitor low, require MFA or remediation at medium, block high
Engineering Notes: Risk-based controls require appropriate Microsoft Entra licensing.

Customer Question: Which public IPs are corporate locations, and which countries should be monitored or blocked?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines named locations and geographic policies.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Corporate IPs; operating countries; prohibited countries; traveler exception process
Configuration Impact: Configures named locations and location-based policies
Default If Undecided: Document corporate IPs but do not bypass MFA; monitor before geographic blocking
Engineering Notes: Maintain an owner and review cadence for public IP changes.

Customer Question: What sign-in frequency and persistent-browser behavior should apply to users and administrators?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines session-control policy values.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Admins every 8 hours and no persistent browser; users 7 days; every time for sensitive action
Configuration Impact: Configures sign-in frequency and persistent-browser session controls
Required Participants: Identity Owner; Business Owners; Service Desk
Default If Undecided: Use service defaults for ordinary users and stricter controls for privileged access
Engineering Notes: Pilot Office desktop, browser and mobile behavior.

Customer Question: What may users do from unmanaged devices?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines whether access is blocked, browser-only or allows limited web access without download.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Block; browser-only; allow web editing but block download; require app protection; unrestricted for low-risk resources
Configuration Impact: Configures Conditional Access, SharePoint access control and session restrictions
Required Participants: Endpoint Owner; Collaboration Owner; Business Leaders
Default If Undecided: Allow restricted browser access to approved low-risk resources and block download
Engineering Notes: Decide separately for employees, contractors, guests and BYOD.

Customer Question: How long must a new Conditional Access policy remain in report-only mode before enforcement?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines the minimum evidence window and implementation schedule.
Expected Answer Type: Number of days plus sign-in volume
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: 7 days; 14 days; 30 days; one full business cycle
Default If Undecided: 14 days and representative sign-in coverage
Engineering Notes: Longer observation may be needed for monthly or seasonal workflows.

Customer Question: Which device platforms and OS versions may enroll in Intune?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines platform restrictions and minimum-version settings.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Windows 11; supported macOS versions; current iOS or iPadOS; Android Enterprise
Default If Undecided: Allow currently supported corporate platforms only
Engineering Notes: Align minimum versions with application compatibility and hardware plans.

Customer Question: Should personal devices be blocked from MDM enrollment, allowed for selected platforms, or supported through app protection only?
Why This Must Be Asked: Directly determines the personal-enrollment restriction and BYOD model.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Block personal Windows and macOS; app protection only for mobile; permit enrolled mobile BYOD; no BYOD
Configuration Impact: Configures Intune enrollment restrictions and BYOD workflows
Required Participants: HR; Legal; Service Desk; Business Leaders
Default If Undecided: Block personal Windows and macOS enrollment and use application protection for approved mobile BYOD
Engineering Notes: Ownership identification must work before blocking personal enrollment.

Customer Question: How many managed devices may each user enroll?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines the Intune device-limit restriction.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: 3; 5; 10; special deployment-account limit
Default If Undecided: Five devices per user
Engineering Notes: Use separate controlled accounts for bulk or shared-device provisioning.

Customer Question: Will Windows devices be Entra joined, hybrid joined, registered, or use multiple approved models?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines enrollment, Autopilot, authentication and device-compliance design.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Entra joined; hybrid joined; registered BYOD; shared-device profile
Default If Undecided: Use Entra join for new cloud-ready devices and retain hybrid join only where dependencies require it
Engineering Notes: Do not select hybrid join solely because Active Directory exists.

Customer Question: Which Apple devices are corporate owned, personal, supervised, shared or user enrolled?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines Apple Business Manager, enrollment profiles and management authority.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Corporate macOS; corporate supervised iPhone or iPad; personal user enrollment; app protection only
Configuration Impact: Configures Apple enrollment tokens and profiles
Default If Undecided: Use Apple Business Manager for corporate devices and app protection or user enrollment for approved BYOD
Engineering Notes: Confirm ownership through Apple Business Manager or procurement records.

Customer Question: Which conditions make a Windows device compliant?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines the exact Intune compliance-policy settings.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Supported OS; BitLocker; Secure Boot; firewall; antivirus; code integrity; Defender risk at or below Medium
Default If Undecided: Require supported OS, encryption, firewall, antivirus, Secure Boot and Defender risk at or below Low or Medium based on risk tolerance
Engineering Notes: Confirm all required settings can be measured reliably.

Customer Question: How long should users have to remediate ordinary compliance failures?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines noncompliance actions and eventual access blocking.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Immediate; 1 day; 3 days; 7 days
Default If Undecided: Three-day grace period for ordinary failures and immediate action for high-risk devices
Engineering Notes: Separate policy failure from active-threat signals.

Customer Question: Should the Microsoft security baseline be applied largely as published or adjusted for application compatibility?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines whether the baseline is enforced uniformly or uses customer-specific settings.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Microsoft defaults; stricter customer standard; compatibility-adjusted baseline
Required Participants: Endpoint Owner; Application Owners; Service Desk
Default If Undecided: Apply reviewed Microsoft baseline with documented compatibility exceptions
Engineering Notes: Every changed setting should retain rationale.

Customer Question: Which applications must be installed, available, prohibited or removed from managed devices?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines Intune application assignments and application-control design.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Required; Available; Uninstall; Prohibited; department specific
Configuration Impact: Configures application assignments and packaging backlog
Default If Undecided: Deploy core security and productivity applications as required; make approved optional apps available
Engineering Notes: Assign an owner and support process to every required application.

Customer Question: Which applications and policies must complete before a new Windows device may be used?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines ESP blocking applications and acceptable provisioning duration.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Security agent; Office; VPN; RMM; compliance policy; certificate
Default If Undecided: Block only on critical security, management and productivity components
Engineering Notes: Too many blocking applications increase provisioning failures.

Customer Question: Which devices and platforms must be onboarded to Microsoft Defender?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines onboarding methods, licensing and device groups.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Windows clients; Windows servers; macOS; Linux; mobile; unmanaged servers through security settings management
Required Participants: Endpoint Owner; Infrastructure Owner; Licensing Owner
Default If Undecided: Onboard all supported corporate endpoints and approved servers
Engineering Notes: Document incompatible third-party EDR and unsupported systems.

Customer Question: Will Microsoft Defender Antivirus be primary, passive, or replaced by another approved product?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines antivirus policy, EDR block mode and third-party removal sequence.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Defender primary; Defender passive with third-party AV; third-party only; migration state
Default If Undecided: Use Defender as primary after validated third-party removal
Engineering Notes: Avoid running unsupported combinations of real-time antivirus engines.

Customer Question: Which applications require Defender exclusions, and who must approve them?
Why This Must Be Asked: Broad exclusions can create significant security gaps.
Expected Answer Type: Exception list with exact paths, processes, extensions and owners
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Vendor-documented server exclusion; database path; backup process
Required Participants: Application Owners; Vendors; Endpoint Security Engineer
Default If Undecided: No exclusions except Microsoft or vendor-documented requirements validated by security
Engineering Notes: Use the narrowest supported exclusion.

Customer Question: How much automated investigation and remediation may Defender perform on user devices and servers?
