Why This Must Be Asked: Determines device-group automation levels and operational response.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Full automation; semi-automatic; approval required; no automatic remediation
Configuration Impact: Configures Defender device groups and automation
Required Participants: Security Operations; Endpoint Owner; Infrastructure Owner
Default If Undecided: Use full or semi-automatic remediation for user endpoints and more controlled settings for critical servers
Engineering Notes: Validate operational recovery and exception procedure.

Customer Question: Which applications or device classes require inbound firewall rules?
Why This Must Be Asked: Default inbound blocking requires an approved exception inventory.
Expected Answer Type: Rule list by application and profile
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Remote support; management systems; approved peer services; server applications
Default If Undecided: Block unsolicited inbound traffic and permit only documented required services
Engineering Notes: Scope by executable, service, address, port and network profile.

Customer Question: Which drives must be encrypted, what encryption method is required, and where will recovery keys be stored?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines disk-encryption policy and recovery support.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: OS drives; fixed data drives; removable drives; XTS-AES 128 or approved value; Entra escrow
Default If Undecided: Encrypt OS and fixed corporate drives and escrow keys to Entra ID
Engineering Notes: Validate recovery before broad enforcement.

Customer Question: Who may retrieve BitLocker recovery keys, and what identity-verification process is required?
Why This Must Be Asked: Recovery keys provide access to encrypted data and must be restricted.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Service desk through ticket and identity verification; endpoint administrators; security only
Configuration Impact: Configures Entra roles and support procedure
Default If Undecided: Restrict retrieval to authorized support personnel with a ticket and identity verification
Engineering Notes: Audit recovery-key retrieval where available.

Customer Question: Which users or support roles require local administrator access?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines LAPS, local-group membership and privilege-removal scope.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: No users; support team only; developers by exception; temporary elevation
Configuration Impact: Configures local administrator membership and support workflow
Required Participants: Application Owners; Development Leaders; Service Desk
Default If Undecided: Remove ordinary users and provide support access through Windows LAPS or approved elevation
Engineering Notes: Developer exceptions should remain device-scoped and time-bound where possible.

Customer Question: Where should LAPS credentials be backed up, how often should they rotate, and who may retrieve them?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines exact Windows LAPS policy values.
Expected Answer Type: Directory, rotation period and authorized roles
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Entra ID backup; Active Directory backup; 7-day rotation; 30-day rotation; rotate after use
Required Participants: Endpoint Owner; Identity Owner; Service Desk
Default If Undecided: Back up to Entra ID for Entra-joined devices, rotate every 30 days and after use, and restrict retrieval
Engineering Notes: Avoid competing LAPS configurations.

Customer Question: Which ASR rules should be audited, warned or blocked, and what pilot period is required?
Why This Must Be Asked: Individual rules can affect different applications and workflows.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Audit; Warn; Block; Not applicable
Configuration Impact: Configures ASR policies and rollout waves
Default If Undecided: Audit all applicable rules, then move validated rules individually to block
Engineering Notes: Do not enforce the entire rule set at once without application telemetry.

Customer Question: Does the customer want monitoring, a managed-installer model or strict application allowlisting?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines App Control for Business design and required application inventory quality.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Audit only; managed installer trust; publisher allowlist; strict allowlisting
Required Participants: Application Owner; Endpoint Owner; Business Leaders
Default If Undecided: Begin in audit and use managed installers or publisher rules before strict allowlisting
Engineering Notes: Strict enforcement requires mature packaging and emergency recovery.

Customer Question: Which departments or applications require Office macros, trusted locations or trusted publishers?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines macro restrictions and exceptions.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: No macros; signed macros only; trusted publisher; approved trusted location; department exception
Default If Undecided: Block internet-originated macros and allow only documented signed or trusted business macros
Engineering Notes: Users should not be able to create their own broadly writable trusted locations.

Customer Question: Which browsers and extensions are approved for organizational use?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines managed-browser policy and extension allowlist.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Microsoft Edge only; Edge and Chrome; approved password manager; accessibility extensions; blocked extension categories
Configuration Impact: Configures browser policies and extension controls
Default If Undecided: Manage Microsoft Edge and block unapproved extensions
Engineering Notes: Review existing extensions before moving to allowlist enforcement.

Customer Question: Will USB and other removable storage be blocked, read-only, encrypted-only or permitted?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines Defender Device Control and Endpoint DLP behavior.
Expected Answer Type: Policy by user or device group
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Block all; read-only; approved device identifiers; encrypted devices only; unrestricted with auditing
Default If Undecided: Audit first, then block unapproved storage and permit approved encrypted devices
Engineering Notes: Identify backup, manufacturing, medical and other specialized workflows.

Customer Question: Which websites, categories or applications require exceptions from network protection or reputation controls?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines network-protection mode and web exceptions.
Expected Answer Type: URL or category list with owner
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Business SaaS false positive; internal site; vendor download site
Default If Undecided: No exceptions unless a verified business site is incorrectly blocked
Engineering Notes: Use exact destinations and expiration rather than broad category exclusions.

Customer Question: Should the organization use Standard protection, Strict protection, custom policies, or a combination by user group?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines anti-spam and threat-policy architecture.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Standard for all users; Strict for executives and priority accounts; custom policies for special workflows
Configuration Impact: Configures preset and custom security policies
Default If Undecided: Apply Standard broadly and Strict to priority users after pilot validation
Engineering Notes: Avoid overlapping policies with unclear precedence.

Customer Question: Which attachment types must be blocked, quarantined or allowed?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines anti-malware common attachment filtering.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Executables blocked; archives scanned; macro files quarantined; approved business file exceptions
Default If Undecided: Block Microsoft-recommended high-risk attachment types
Engineering Notes: Use secure file transfer for business processes that require prohibited file types.

Customer Question: Which executives, departments, brand names and domains require impersonation protection?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines anti-phishing protected-user and protected-domain entries.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Executives; finance; payroll; HR; IT; major customer-facing domains
Default If Undecided: Protect executives, finance, payroll, HR and IT leadership
Engineering Notes: Review the protected list after personnel changes.

Customer Question: Should suspicious attachments be blocked, replaced, dynamically delivered or monitored?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines attachment detonation and delivery behavior.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Dynamic Delivery; Block; Replace; Monitor
Default If Undecided: Use Dynamic Delivery or block based on validated user experience and risk
Engineering Notes: Test mobile, shared mailbox and automated-processing scenarios.

Customer Question: Should Safe Links protect email, Teams and supported Office applications, and should users be allowed to click through warnings?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines URL rewriting, time-of-click scanning and user override behavior.
Expected Answer Type: Yes or No per workload and override
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Email; Teams; Office apps; no user click-through; click-through with warning
Required Participants: Messaging Owner; Collaboration Owner; Service Desk
Default If Undecided: Enable supported workloads and prevent bypass of high-confidence malicious links
Engineering Notes: Document narrow URL exceptions separately.

Customer Question: Which platforms are authorized to send email using each customer domain?
Why This Must Be Asked: SPF, DKIM and DMARC cannot be safely enforced without a complete sender inventory.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Exchange Online; marketing platform; ticketing system; website; scanners; payroll platform
Required Participants: DNS Owner; Application Owners; Marketing; Vendors
Default If Undecided: Include only validated active senders and treat unknown sources as remediation items
Engineering Notes: Capture envelope and header domains and whether the sender supports DKIM.

Customer Question: What DMARC policy and implementation timeline does the customer approve?
Why This Must Be Asked: Moving directly to reject without validating senders can disrupt legitimate mail.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: p=none; p=quarantine; p=reject; gradual pct rollout
Configuration Impact: Configures DMARC DNS record and reporting
Default If Undecided: Start at monitoring, validate all sources, then progress to quarantine and reject
Engineering Notes: Define who reviews aggregate reports.

Customer Question: Which users, applications or mailboxes legitimately send high volumes of email?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines outbound spam limits and bulk-sender exceptions.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Marketing platform; alerting system; ticketing system; executive assistant
Configuration Impact: Configures outbound spam policy and alternate sending design
Default If Undecided: Use a dedicated bulk-mail service rather than broad Exchange Online exceptions
Engineering Notes: Compromised-account detection should not be weakened for normal users.

Customer Question: Should automatic external forwarding ever be permitted?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines outbound-spam policy, transport rules and mailbox-forwarding exceptions.
Expected Answer Type: Yes or No plus approved cases
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Block all; allow approved business workflows; allow only partner domains
Default If Undecided: Block automatic external forwarding
Engineering Notes: Approved exceptions need destination, data type, owner and expiration.

Customer Question: Which devices and applications require SMTP AUTH, relay or Direct Send?
Why This Must Be Asked: Disabling legacy sending paths can break scanners and applications.
Expected Answer Type: Device and application inventory with target method
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: OAuth SMTP; authenticated relay; connector relay; Azure Communication Services; third-party relay; retire
Configuration Impact: Configures organization SMTP AUTH and mailbox exceptions
Default If Undecided: Disable SMTP AUTH globally and allow only documented temporary exceptions
Engineering Notes: Direct Send and relay choices must consider spoofing and recipient scope.

Customer Question: Where should user-reported phishing and suspicious messages be routed?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines submissions workflow and analyst responsibility.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Microsoft and security team; security team only; monitored mailbox; ITSM queue
Default If Undecided: Send reports to Microsoft and a restricted internal security queue
Engineering Notes: Define response expectations for users who report messages.

Customer Question: What is the maximum external-sharing level allowed for the tenant?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines the ceiling for every SharePoint and OneDrive site.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Only people in organization; existing guests only; new and existing guests; Anyone
Default If Undecided: Allow new and existing authenticated guests; disable Anyone by default
Engineering Notes: Sensitive sites should be more restrictive than the tenant maximum.

Customer Question: Which site types may collaborate externally?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines site-level sharing settings.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: No external sharing; approved partner sites; client project sites; public marketing sites
Default If Undecided: Disable external sharing for sensitive sites and allow authenticated sharing only for approved collaboration sites
Engineering Notes: Assign a business owner to every externally shared site.

Customer Question: May users share OneDrive content externally, or must external collaboration occur in governed SharePoint or Teams sites?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines OneDrive sharing and user behavior.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: No external sharing; authenticated guests; approved departments; temporary project use
Default If Undecided: Restrict OneDrive external sharing and direct longer-term collaboration to governed sites
Engineering Notes: OneDrive should not become an unmanaged team repository.

Customer Question: What may guests do in Teams meetings, chat, calling, applications and file collaboration?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines Teams guest settings and support expectations.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Allow chat; allow channel access; restrict calling; restrict application installation; restrict meeting control
Default If Undecided: Allow required collaboration but restrict unnecessary calling, application and meeting-control capabilities
Engineering Notes: Align Teams and SharePoint guest behavior.

Customer Question: Will Anyone links be allowed anywhere in the tenant?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines anonymous-sharing settings and remediation scope.
Expected Answer Type: Yes or No plus site exceptions
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Disabled tenant-wide; approved public sites only; selected departments; unrestricted
Default If Undecided: Disable Anyone links except explicitly approved public-content sites
Engineering Notes: Anyone links do not identify recipients.

Customer Question: How long should approved anonymous links remain active?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines link-expiration settings and monitoring.
Configuration Impact: Configures maximum expiration for Anyone links
Default If Undecided: Expire within 14 days
Engineering Notes: Users can issue a shorter expiration than the maximum.

Customer Question: Should the default link be Specific people or organization-only, and should it default to View or Edit?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines safer user-sharing behavior.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Specific people and View; organization-only and View; specific people and Edit
Configuration Impact: Configures SharePoint and OneDrive default links
Default If Undecided: Specific people with View permission
Engineering Notes: Users can deliberately select Edit where policy permits.

Customer Question: Should external collaboration use approved-domain allowlists, prohibited-domain blocklists or no domain restrictions?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines SharePoint, Teams and Entra domain lists.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Allowlist; blocklist; no restrictions; site-specific restrictions
Default If Undecided: Use a blocklist for known prohibited domains unless the customer can reliably maintain an allowlist
Engineering Notes: Assign an owner and review cadence.

Customer Question: Which domains and domain controllers should receive Defender for Identity sensors?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines sensor deployment scope and licensing.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: All production domain controllers; federation servers; AD CS servers where supported
Default If Undecided: Deploy to all supported production domain controllers
Engineering Notes: Validate sizing, connectivity and service account requirements.

Customer Question: How should NTLM, LDAP simple bind, unsigned LDAP, SMB weaknesses and other legacy identity findings be handled?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines whether findings are remediated, isolated or accepted.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Block; migrate; isolate; monitor; temporary exception
Default If Undecided: Inventory and remediate dependencies before enforcement
Engineering Notes: Each exception needs owner and retirement date.

Customer Question: Which endpoint, firewall or proxy sources may be used for Cloud App Discovery?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines discovery coverage and connector architecture.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Defender endpoint telemetry; firewall logs; proxy logs; log collector; no discovery
Default If Undecided: Use Defender endpoint telemetry where licensed and supplement with network sources as needed
Engineering Notes: Review data residency and privacy requirements.

Customer Question: At what risk score or condition must a discovered cloud application be reviewed or blocked?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines application-triage thresholds.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Review below score 7; block high-risk unsanctioned apps; review apps accessing sensitive data
Configuration Impact: Configures governance workflow and possible blocking
Default If Undecided: Review high-use or high-risk apps and block only after business impact validation unless actively malicious
Engineering Notes: Risk score should be combined with usage and data sensitivity.

Customer Question: May users consent to applications, and under what conditions?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines user-consent restrictions and admin-consent workflow.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Disable user consent; verified publishers and low-risk permissions only; unrestricted; selected users only
Default If Undecided: Allow only verified publishers and low-impact permissions, with admin workflow for all others
Engineering Notes: A restrictive model requires timely application review.

Customer Question: Who reviews application consent requests, and what response time is expected?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines approvers, workflow duration and escalation.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Security team; application review board; identity team; 2 business days
Default If Undecided: Use multiple security and application reviewers with a defined response target
Engineering Notes: Review permission scope, publisher, terms, business owner and data access.

Decision or Topic: Defender for Cloud Apps session control
Customer Question: Which applications and scenarios require real-time session restrictions?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines Conditional Access App Control scope.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Block downloads from unmanaged devices; monitor sensitive app sessions; protect admin portals
Configuration Impact: Configures Defender for Cloud Apps session policies
Default If Undecided: Pilot selected sensitive web applications and unmanaged-device download restrictions
Engineering Notes: Reverse-proxy compatibility must be tested per application.

Customer Question: Which workloads and actions must be available for investigation and compliance?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines audit validation scenarios and evidence requirements.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Entra roles; mailbox access; sharing; Teams changes; Intune policies; DLP; Copilot
Default If Undecided: Validate all deployed Microsoft 365 security, administrative and compliance workloads
Engineering Notes: Document events unavailable because of platform or licensing limits.

Customer Question: How long must sign-in, audit, provisioning, risk, Defender and compliance logs be retained?
Why This Must Be Asked: Directly determines native retention, Purview Audit retention, Log Analytics, storage and SIEM settings.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: 30 days; 90 days; 180 days; 1 year; 7 years
Configuration Impact: Configures GBL-P1-ALM-004 and related logging destinations
Default If Undecided: Retain security logs for at least one year where licensing and budget permit; otherwise document achievable native and exported retention
Engineering Notes: Separate operational security retention from legally required evidence retention.

Customer Question: Where should identity and security logs be stored or forwarded?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines diagnostic settings, access control, cost and investigation process.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Microsoft Sentinel; Log Analytics; storage account; third-party SIEM; native portals only
Configuration Impact: Configures Entra diagnostic settings and integrations
Required Participants: Azure Owner; Compliance; Finance; Security Operations
Default If Undecided: Use the approved SIEM or Log Analytics workspace and archive where longer retention is required
Engineering Notes: Document subscription ownership, region, access and cost center.

Customer Question: Do regulated or investigation logs require immutable storage or a separate archive?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines storage-account immutability, archive tiers or external evidence storage.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Immutable for one year; archive for seven years; no separate archive
Default If Undecided: Use access-controlled exported logs and add immutability only when legally or contractually required
Engineering Notes: Immutability can increase cost and complicate correction or deletion requirements.

Customer Question: Who receives low, medium, high and critical alerts, and how quickly must each severity be addressed?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines notification rules, ticket routing and operational commitments.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Critical 15 minutes; high 1 hour; medium 1 business day; low review queue
Required Participants: Service Manager; Executive Sponsor; Workload Owners
Default If Undecided: Route critical and high alerts to the security queue and define business-hours handling for lower severities
Engineering Notes: Do not configure an SLA that the service is not staffed to meet.

Customer Question: Should security alerts create ITSM tickets automatically, and for which severities?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines automation, duplicate handling and incident ownership.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Critical and high auto-ticket; medium alert queue; low dashboard only
Default If Undecided: Automatically create tickets for high and critical actionable alerts
Engineering Notes: Define deduplication and incident synchronization.

Customer Question: Does the customer want a target Secure Score or a risk-based review without a fixed percentage?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines reporting expectations and prioritization.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Target 70 percent; target 80 percent; improve quarterly; no fixed target
Configuration Impact: Shapes monthly review and leadership reporting
Default If Undecided: Use risk-based recommendation review rather than treating the percentage as the sole objective
Engineering Notes: Some recommendations may be inapplicable or blocked by licensing.

Customer Question: What minimum conditions must be satisfied before Phase 1 is considered complete?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines whether engineering can close implementation and transfer controls to operations.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: MFA coverage; tested emergency accounts; CA enforced; Defender coverage; device compliance; email controls; logging operational
Required Participants: Technical Lead; Service Manager; Workstream Owners
Default If Undecided: Require validated foundational controls, evidence, support handoff and approved residual risks
Engineering Notes: Items blocked by license or dependency require explicit disposition.

Customer Question: What information-classification levels should the organization use?
Why This Must Be Asked: Engineers cannot design sensitivity labels, encryption, DLP, sharing restrictions or handling requirements until the business taxonomy is approved.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Public; Internal; Confidential; Highly Confidential; Restricted
Configuration Impact: Determines the sensitivity-label hierarchy, handling matrix, DLP severity and access controls
Required Participants: Security; Legal; Compliance; Privacy; Business Data Owners
Default If Undecided: Use Public, Internal, Confidential and Highly Confidential as the initial proposal
Engineering Notes: Each classification should produce a meaningful difference in handling or protection.

Phase: Phase 2 - Data Protection, Governance & AI Readiness
Customer Question: What content belongs in each classification level?
Why This Must Be Asked: Users and automatic classifiers need clear criteria for selecting the correct classification.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Public marketing material; internal procedures; customer contracts; regulated records; credentials
Configuration Impact: Determines user guidance, classifier design, label descriptions and training
Default If Undecided: Use business examples gathered during Phase 0 and refine through the pilot
Engineering Notes: Avoid definitions based only on abstract terms such as important or sensitive.

Phase: Phase 2 - Data Protection, Governance & AI Readiness
Customer Question: What storage, sharing, encryption, printing, copying and disposal rules apply to each classification?
Why This Must Be Asked: The label name alone does not tell engineers what technical controls it must apply.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: External sharing allowed; named recipients only; encryption required; printing prohibited; removable media prohibited
Configuration Impact: Determines label actions, DLP restrictions, Endpoint DLP rules and sharing controls
Required Participants: Legal; Privacy; Business Data Owners; Collaboration Owner
Default If Undecided: Use progressively stronger protection as classification sensitivity increases
Engineering Notes: Separate mandatory technical controls from user guidance.

Phase: Phase 2 - Data Protection, Governance & AI Readiness
Customer Question: Who is accountable for each major data domain?
Why This Must Be Asked: Data owners must approve classification, access, retention, sharing, remediation and AI grounding decisions.
Expected Answer Type: Named owner and steward by data domain
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: HR Director; Finance Director; Legal Counsel; Sales Operations; Information Security
Configuration Impact: Determines owner certification, approval workflows and exception routing
Customer Decision Owner: Executive Sponsor or Data Governance Owner
Default If Undecided: Assign department leaders as interim owners until formally delegated
Engineering Notes: Use named individuals with backup owners rather than department names alone.

Phase: Phase 2 - Data Protection, Governance & AI Readiness
Customer Question: Which regulated and contractual data types does the organization process or store?
Why This Must Be Asked: Engineers need to select only relevant sensitive information types and controls.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Social Security numbers; payment-card data; health information; tax data; financial account data; student data; export-controlled data
Configuration Impact: Determines built-in sensitive information types, DLP rules, alert severity and retention requirements
Default If Undecided: Enable only data types confirmed as applicable and use discovery to identify additional candidates
Engineering Notes: Record jurisdiction and regulatory basis where applicable.

Phase: Phase 2 - Data Protection, Governance & AI Readiness
Customer Question: Does the organization have proprietary identifiers or document patterns that require custom detection?
Why This Must Be Asked: Built-in Microsoft classifiers may not recognize customer-specific records.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Employee number; client account number; claim number; project code; contract number
Configuration Impact: Determines custom sensitive information types and supporting evidence logic
Required Participants: Application Owners; Data Owners; Purview Engineer
Default If Undecided: Do not create custom types unless built-in detection is insufficient
Engineering Notes: Use synthetic or sanitized samples for testing whenever possible.

Phase: Phase 2 - Data Protection, Governance & AI Readiness
Customer Question: Are there authoritative structured datasets suitable for Exact Data Match?
Why This Must Be Asked: Exact Data Match requires maintained source data, stable identifiers and secure refresh procedures.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Employee records; customer records; patient records; account numbers; membership records
Configuration Impact: Determines whether Exact Data Match schemas and data uploads are created
Required Participants: Security; Privacy; Database Owner; Purview Engineer
Evidence Required: Approved Exact Data Match source register
Default If Undecided: Use pattern-based detection until an authoritative and governed source is approved
Engineering Notes: Define refresh ownership and source-data protection before implementation.

Phase: Phase 2 - Data Protection, Governance & AI Readiness
Customer Question: Which unstructured document categories need trainable classifiers because patterns and keywords are insufficient?
Why This Must Be Asked: Trainable classifiers require representative examples, validation effort and business ownership.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Contracts; resumes; legal opinions; source code; statements of work; incident reports
Configuration Impact: Determines trainable classifier configuration and validation scope
Required Participants: Legal; Department Data Owners; Purview Engineer
Default If Undecided: Use trainable classifiers only for high-value categories that cannot be detected reliably by simpler methods
Engineering Notes: Confirm that training and validation samples may be used for this purpose.

Phase: Phase 2 - Data Protection, Governance & AI Readiness
Customer Question: What minimum precision and coverage must a classifier achieve before enforcement?
Why This Must Be Asked: Engineers need an acceptance threshold for false positives and missed detections.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: 90 percent precision; 80 percent coverage; advisory use only until threshold is met
Configuration Impact: Determines whether a classifier can be used for auto-labeling, DLP or discovery only
Default If Undecided: Keep the classifier in discovery mode until business owners validate acceptable accuracy
Engineering Notes: Use stricter accuracy expectations when the policy will block user activity.

Phase: Phase 2 - Data Protection, Governance & AI Readiness
Customer Question: What label names, order, scopes and sublabels should appear to users?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines the exact label taxonomy and user experience.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Public; Internal; Confidential; Highly Confidential with HR, Legal or Finance sublabels
Configuration Impact: Configures sensitivity-label names, priority, scope and descriptions
Required Participants: Security; Legal; Department Data Owners; Change Manager
Default If Undecided: Use the approved four-level taxonomy without sublabels unless a sublabel produces a distinct technical outcome
Engineering Notes: Avoid department-named labels when the same protection outcome can be reused.

Phase: Phase 2 - Data Protection, Governance & AI Readiness
Customer Question: Which labels should apply to files and email, meetings, groups and sites, or data assets?
Why This Must Be Asked: Different workloads support different protection outcomes and user experiences.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Files and email only; files, email and meetings; groups and sites; all supported scopes
Required Participants: Collaboration Owner; Messaging Owner; Purview Engineer
Default If Undecided: Apply document labels to files and email and use separate container labels for groups and sites
Engineering Notes: Do not combine scopes unless the label's protection outcomes remain understandable.

Phase: Phase 2 - Data Protection, Governance & AI Readiness
Customer Question: Which users, departments and data owners should receive sensitivity labels first?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines pilot assignment and the quality of business feedback.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: IT; Legal; HR; Finance; compliance team; selected champions
Required Participants: Department Leaders; Change Manager; Service Desk
Default If Undecided: Use a representative group from IT, legal, HR and ordinary business users
Engineering Notes: Include users who work with both internal and externally shared content.

Phase: Phase 2 - Data Protection, Governance & AI Readiness
Customer Question: Should newly created files and email receive a default label, and which label should it be?
Why This Must Be Asked: A default increases label coverage but can misclassify content or create user confusion.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Internal by default; Public by default; no default; department-specific defaults
Configuration Impact: Configures default-label settings in publishing policies
Required Participants: Security; Business Data Owners; Change Manager
Default If Undecided: Use a nonrestrictive Internal label in the pilot if approved; otherwise no default until usage is understood
Engineering Notes: Avoid an encrypted default label without extensive compatibility testing.

Phase: Phase 2 - Data Protection, Governance & AI Readiness
Customer Question: Should users be required to label files, email, meetings or other supported content?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines mandatory-label settings and user impact.
Expected Answer Type: Yes or No by workload and persona
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Mandatory for documents; mandatory for email; selected departments only; default label without mandatory labeling
Required Participants: Security; Legal; Department Leaders; Change Manager
Default If Undecided: Pilot default labeling first and enable mandatory labeling only after training and validation
Engineering Notes: System-generated and automated content may require exceptions.

Phase: Phase 2 - Data Protection, Governance & AI Readiness
Customer Question: Should users be required to justify lowering or removing a sensitivity label?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines downgrade controls and audit requirements.
Expected Answer Type: Yes or No plus affected users
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Require for all users; require for Confidential and above; not required
Default If Undecided: Require justification for lowering or removing a label
Engineering Notes: Review repeated downgrade reasons to identify policy or training issues.

Phase: Phase 2 - Data Protection, Governance & AI Readiness
Customer Question: Which labels should force Teams, Microsoft 365 Groups and SharePoint sites to Public or Private?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines container-label privacy settings.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Public label allows public group; Internal defaults private; Confidential requires private
Default If Undecided: Require private workspaces for Confidential and higher classifications
Engineering Notes: Public workspaces should require explicit business-owner approval.

Phase: Phase 2 - Data Protection, Governance & AI Readiness
Customer Question: Which workspace classifications may include guests?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines container-label external-user access behavior.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Public and Internal permit guests; Confidential by exception; Highly Confidential prohibits guests
Configuration Impact: Configures guest-access controls for labeled containers
Default If Undecided: Prohibit guests for Highly Confidential workspaces and require approval for Confidential workspaces
Engineering Notes: Align this with tenant and site external-sharing controls.

Phase: Phase 2 - Data Protection, Governance & AI Readiness
Customer Question: Which labeled sites may be accessed or downloaded from unmanaged devices?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines container-label and SharePoint access restrictions.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Full access; browser-only; block download; block all access
Required Participants: Collaboration Owner; Endpoint Owner; Business Data Owners
Default If Undecided: Block download for Confidential and block access for Highly Confidential unless an approved business requirement exists
Engineering Notes: Test browser editing, synchronization and mobile behavior.

Phase: Phase 2 - Data Protection, Governance & AI Readiness
Customer Question: Should DLP policies be organized by data type, regulation, business process, workload or severity?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines naming, policy structure, rule precedence and operational ownership.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Enterprise policy by data type; regulatory policies; workload policies; hybrid model
Default If Undecided: Use reusable policies by data type and risk, with workload-specific rules where supported behavior differs
Engineering Notes: Avoid duplicate conditions across many policies.

Phase: Phase 2 - Data Protection, Governance & AI Readiness
Customer Question: Who should receive DLP alerts and incident reports for each severity and data type?
Why This Must Be Asked: DLP alerts can contain sensitive evidence and need accountable investigators.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Security Operations; Compliance; Privacy; HR; data owner; dedicated DLP analysts
Configuration Impact: Configures alert recipients, role groups and ticket routing
Required Participants: Privacy; Legal; Service Manager; Data Owners
Default If Undecided: Route alerts to a restricted data-security or compliance queue and involve data owners as needed
Engineering Notes: Do not send matched-content evidence to broad distribution lists.

Phase: Phase 2 - Data Protection, Governance & AI Readiness
Customer Question: Who may approve a DLP exception, how long may it last, and what compensating controls are required?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines policy exclusions and exception workflow.

Configuration Impact: Configures exception register and policy exclusions
Default If Undecided: Require data-owner and security approval with an expiration no longer than 90 days
Engineering Notes: Prefer narrow user, site, destination or activity exceptions.

Phase: Phase 2 - Data Protection, Governance & AI Readiness
Customer Question: Which sensitive information must be restricted when sent externally?

Default If Undecided: Start with the highest-risk confirmed data types and external recipients
Engineering Notes: Include approved partner domains and encrypted sharing workflows.

Phase: Phase 2 - Data Protection, Governance & AI Readiness
Customer Question: When should an agent be disabled or retired?

Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Owner departure; no use for 90 days; expired purpose; unsupported connector; security incident; replacement published
Configuration Impact: Configures agent certification and retirement workflow
Required Participants: Business Owner; Security; Power Platform Administrator
Default If Undecided: Review inactive agents after 90 days and retire ownerless or unapproved agents
Engineering Notes: Retirement includes connectors, credentials, flows and data-source access.

Phase: Phase 2 - Data Protection, Governance & AI Readiness
Customer Question: Who writes and approves sensitivity-label, DLP, retention and AI user messages?

Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Change team drafts; security validates; legal approves; customer communications publishes
Configuration Impact: Configures policy tips and launch communications
Required Participants: Legal; Security; Data Governance; Service Desk
Default If Undecided: Engineering drafts technical text and customer communications approves user-facing language
Engineering Notes: Policy messages should contain an approved alternative action and support path.

Phase: Phase 2 - Data Protection, Governance & AI Readiness
Customer Question: Which users, owners, reviewers, investigators, administrators and agent makers require training?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines training scope and phase acceptance.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: All users; data owners; DLP analysts; records reviewers; legal investigators; service desk; agent makers
Configuration Impact: Creates training plan and access prerequisites
Default If Undecided: Train every role that receives new responsibility or encounters new controls
Engineering Notes: Administrative access should not be assigned before required training is complete.

Phase: Phase 2 - Data Protection, Governance & AI Readiness
Customer Question: Must training be completed before access, policy enforcement or production agent publication?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines rollout gates and evidence requirements.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: End users before mandatory labeling; analysts before case access; makers before publication
Configuration Impact: Controls role assignment and rollout timing
Default If Undecided: Require training before privileged operational access or agent publication and before broad user enforcement where practical
Engineering Notes: Track remediation for incomplete training.

Phase: Phase 2 - Data Protection, Governance & AI Readiness
Customer Question: Which team handles first-line support for sensitivity labels, DLP blocks, retention, guest access and AI incidents?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines ticket routing and escalation.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Service desk; security operations; compliance; records team; collaboration team; AI governance
Configuration Impact: Configures ITSM categories and escalation paths
Default If Undecided: Service desk performs intake and routes security, compliance and records decisions to the accountable team
Engineering Notes: Service desk should not bypass compliance controls to close a ticket.

Phase: Phase 2 - Data Protection, Governance & AI Readiness
Customer Question: How should users request an exception to a label, DLP, retention, sharing or AI policy?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines intake fields, approvals, technical implementation and expiration.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: ITSM form; data-owner approval; security review; legal review; maximum duration
Default If Undecided: Use an ITSM request requiring owner, business reason, control, duration and approvers
Engineering Notes: Retention and legal-hold exceptions require records or legal approval.

Phase: Phase 2 - Data Protection, Governance & AI Readiness
Customer Question: Which security, compliance, governance and AI metrics should be reported to leadership?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines dashboards, data sources and operational reporting.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Label adoption; DLP events; anonymous links; overdue access reviews; agent count; AI incidents; retention failures
Configuration Impact: Configures control dashboards and monthly service report
Required Participants: Security; Compliance; Data Governance; Service Manager
Default If Undecided: Report trends, high-risk exceptions, overdue remediation and control adoption
Engineering Notes: Avoid reporting raw event volume without business context.

Phase: Phase 2 - Data Protection, Governance & AI Readiness
Customer Question: What metric values should trigger investigation, escalation or policy review?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines alert thresholds and governance actions.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: DLP false positives over 5 percent; anonymous links over zero in sensitive sites; review completion below 90 percent
Default If Undecided: Escalate critical exposure immediately and review deteriorating trends monthly
Engineering Notes: Thresholds should be reviewed after the first operating quarter.

Phase: Phase 2 - Data Protection, Governance & AI Readiness
Customer Question: Which business workflows and negative tests must pass before enforcement?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines the control test plan and acceptance evidence.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Internal sharing; approved partner sharing; prohibited recipient; printing; USB; agent access; legal hold; label downgrade
Required Participants: Data Owners; Security; Compliance; Business Users
Default If Undecided: Test normal use, approved exception, blocked use, attempted bypass and rollback
Engineering Notes: Use synthetic sensitive data unless production data is specifically authorized.

Phase: Phase 2 - Data Protection, Governance & AI Readiness
Customer Question: How long must controls operate before they are considered effective?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines provisional versus final acceptance.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: 30 days; 90 days; one business quarter
Default If Undecided: Use at least 30 days for ordinary controls and 90 days where recurring workflows must be observed
Engineering Notes: A successful configuration test does not prove sustained operation.

Phase: Phase 2 - Data Protection, Governance & AI Readiness
Customer Question: Who can accept deployed controls, operational handoff, blocked-by-license items, exceptions and residual risk?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines the formal phase gate and prevents unapproved closure.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Executive Sponsor; Security Owner; Compliance Owner; Data Governance Owner; Legal; Service Owner
Configuration Impact: Controls Phase 2 closure and transition to operations
Required Participants: Technical Lead; Security; Compliance; Data Governance; Service Owner
Default If Undecided: Require technical, security, compliance, data-governance and operational approval
Engineering Notes: Deferred controls need an owner, target date and interim risk treatment.

Customer Question: Which Microsoft 365 and non-Microsoft repositories may be scanned for sensitive and regulated data?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines the authorized scan boundary, required connectors, licensing and assessment coverage.
Expected Answer Type: Repository list with owners and exclusions
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Exchange; SharePoint; OneDrive; Teams; file shares; SQL; Azure storage; Dataverse; third-party cloud repositories
Configuration Impact: Configures discovery tools, connectors, scan schedules and evidence scope
Required Participants: Security; Privacy; Legal; Repository Owners; Infrastructure
Default If Undecided: Scan Microsoft 365 priority repositories first and treat connected repositories as pending approval
Engineering Notes: Excluded repositories should remain visible as assessment gaps rather than being silently omitted.

Customer Question: How often should priority repositories be rescanned?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines scan schedules, operational workload and detection freshness.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Daily; weekly; monthly; quarterly; on demand
Configuration Impact: Configures recurring scan schedules and reporting cadence
Default If Undecided: Scan high-risk repositories weekly and lower-risk repositories monthly or quarterly
Engineering Notes: Consider repository size, change frequency, connector impact and licensing.

Customer Question: What identity type and privilege level may scanning connectors use?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines connector authentication, access boundaries and credential-management requirements.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Managed identity; service principal with certificate; workload identity; dedicated account; vendor-managed identity
Configuration Impact: Configures connector identity and least-privileged permissions
Required Participants: Data Platform Owners; Application Owners; Infrastructure
Default If Undecided: Use managed identity or certificate-based service principal with read-only access
Engineering Notes: Avoid long-lived user passwords and shared administrator credentials.

Customer Question: Are there residency, jurisdiction or contractual restrictions on where scan metadata may be processed or stored?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines connector region, service selection and whether some repositories may be scanned centrally.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: United States only; European Union only; no cross-border metadata; regulated repository restrictions
Configuration Impact: Configures service region, connector architecture and repository exclusions
Default If Undecided: Do not connect restricted repositories until residency requirements are validated
Engineering Notes: Classification metadata can itself reveal sensitive business information.

Customer Question: Who may approve changes to the enterprise classification taxonomy?
Why This Must Be Asked: Prevents uncontrolled classifier and label changes that affect DLP, retention and AI behavior.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Data Governance Council; Legal; Security; Records Manager; Executive Sponsor
Configuration Impact: Determines approval workflow and baseline ownership
Default If Undecided: Require Data Governance, Security and Legal approval for material taxonomy changes
Engineering Notes: Minor description changes may use a simplified approval path.

Customer Question: Which business data categories must exist in addition to regulatory classifications?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines business-specific classifiers and data-domain mapping.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Contracts; intellectual property; source code; customer data; employee records; financial forecasts; merger information
Configuration Impact: Configures classifiers, label guidance and DLP conditions
Default If Undecided: Use only categories with an accountable owner and distinct control requirement
Engineering Notes: Avoid creating categories that do not change protection, retention or ownership.

Customer Question: Who owns each custom sensitive information type or trainable classifier?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines who validates accuracy, approves changes and responds to false positives.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Purview engineer plus HR data owner; security engineer plus legal owner
Configuration Impact: Populates classifier register and change workflow
Required Participants: Purview Engineer; Business Data Owners; Security
Default If Undecided: Do not use unowned custom classifiers in enforcement
Engineering Notes: Ownership must include sample maintenance and accuracy review.

Customer Question: What should happen when a data owner or steward changes roles or leaves?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines automated ownership-transfer, escalation and temporary ownership.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Reassign before termination; manager inherits temporarily; governance team holds ownership; disable affected workflows
Configuration Impact: Configures lifecycle workflow and ownerless-object reporting
Required Participants: Identity Operations; Department Leaders; Collaboration Owner
Default If Undecided: Assign the manager temporarily and require formal reassignment within 30 days
Engineering Notes: Include repositories, groups, applications, agents and policy approvals.

Customer Question: How much representative content must be sampled before a classifier is accepted?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines the confidence of validation and implementation effort.
Expected Answer Type: Sample count or percentage by classifier
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: 100 positive and 100 negative files; 5 percent sample; multiple business units and file types
Required Participants: Business Data Owner; Purview Engineer; Compliance
Default If Undecided: Use a statistically meaningful sample across positive, negative and near-match content
Engineering Notes: Include different languages and file types where applicable.

Customer Question: What precision and coverage must be reached before a classifier can drive auto-labeling or blocking?
Why This Must Be Asked: Prevents unreliable detection from disrupting production workflows.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: 95 percent precision for blocking; 85 percent coverage; no critical false positives
Configuration Impact: Determines whether the classifier is discovery-only, warning-capable or enforceable
Default If Undecided: Keep classifiers in discovery mode until the approved threshold is achieved
Engineering Notes: Blocking commonly requires higher precision than informational discovery.

Customer Question: What label names, descriptions, priority and scopes should become the production standard?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines the final user-visible label experience and policy relationship.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Public; Internal; Confidential; Highly Confidential; Restricted with limited sublabels
Configuration Impact: Configures production sensitivity labels and publishing policies
Required Participants: Security; Legal; Change Manager; Data Owners
Default If Undecided: Use the validated pilot taxonomy and avoid introducing untested labels
Engineering Notes: A new label should produce a distinct handling or protection outcome.

Customer Question: Which languages and accessibility requirements must label names, descriptions and guidance support?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines user-facing text and training content.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: English; French; Spanish; screen-reader-friendly wording; plain-language guidance
Default If Undecided: Publish in the organization's primary business language and add required localizations before regional expansion
Engineering Notes: Use consistent terminology across labels, DLP messages and training.

Customer Question: Which users or groups should retain access to content protected by each encrypted label?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines label encryption permissions and group architecture.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: All employees; department group; named project group; executive group; data-owner-defined audience
Default If Undecided: Use owned groups and the smallest practical approved audience
Engineering Notes: Avoid static individual-user lists where a managed group is possible.

Customer Question: Which external recipients or partner domains may receive encrypted content?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines supported recipient types, identity verification and sharing workflow.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Named external users; approved partner tenants; verified domains; no external recipients
Configuration Impact: Configures encrypted labels and message-encryption policies
Default If Undecided: Allow named recipients from approved partners and prohibit anonymous access
Engineering Notes: Test each external identity type before production rollout.

Customer Question: How long may users access encrypted files without reconnecting to the rights-management service?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines offline access and travel behavior.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: No offline access; 1 day; 7 days; 30 days; never expires
Required Participants: Business Owners; Mobility Owner; Service Desk
Default If Undecided: Use shorter offline access for highly sensitive labels and longer periods only where business travel requires it
Engineering Notes: Test disconnected laptop and mobile scenarios.

Customer Question: Who may use super-user or recovery capabilities to access protected content?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines privileged role assignments, procedures and monitoring.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Compliance administrators; legal operations; security recovery team; two-person approval
Default If Undecided: Restrict recovery access to dedicated privileged accounts under approved change
Engineering Notes: Audit every recovery use.

Customer Question: Should all users see the same labels or should particular roles receive different label policies?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines publication-policy assignments and potential confusion.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Common enterprise labels; executive restricted label; legal sublabels; no specialized labels
Required Participants: Department Data Owners; Change Manager; Purview Engineer
Default If Undecided: Use common enterprise labels and add persona-specific labels only when protection outcomes differ
Engineering Notes: Avoid overlapping policies with conflicting defaults.

Customer Question: When should mandatory labeling become enforceable for each user population?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines rollout waves, communications and support readiness.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Pilot now; IT in 30 days; departments monthly; tenant-wide after 90 days
Configuration Impact: Configures publishing-policy assignments and change schedule
Required Participants: Change Manager; Department Leaders; Service Desk
Default If Undecided: Use staged enforcement only after pilot acceptance and training
Engineering Notes: Confirm supported apps and automated workflows before each wave.

Customer Question: Which desktop, web and mobile clients must support labeling and encryption?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines the test matrix and unsupported-client treatment.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Microsoft 365 Apps for Windows; macOS; Office on the web; iOS; Android; Outlook mobile
Default If Undecided: Validate all supported corporate client platforms and block or remediate unsupported clients
Engineering Notes: Include coauthoring and offline access.

Customer Question: Which partner, consumer and unsupported recipient scenarios must pass before encrypted external sharing is approved?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines external test identities and support documentation.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Partner Entra account; personal Microsoft account; one-time passcode; guest account; unsupported domain
Default If Undecided: Test approved partner identities and one consumer scenario where business use requires it
Engineering Notes: Document unsupported recipient experiences.

Customer Question: Who may approve, modify, disable or bypass a production DLP policy?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines administrative roles and change control.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Purview engineers modify; Data Security approves; emergency disable requires Security Director
Configuration Impact: Configures role assignment and operating procedure
Default If Undecided: Separate policy engineering from approval and exception authority
Engineering Notes: Emergency changes require retrospective review.

Customer Question: Which users and scenarios may override a production DLP restriction?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines override scope, justification and monitoring.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: No overrides; managers only; all users for medium risk; approved departments
Default If Undecided: Allow documented overrides only for approved medium-risk scenarios
Engineering Notes: High-risk regulated data should normally have no user override.

Customer Question: Which workloads should receive production DLP first?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines phased enforcement and support impact.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Exchange first; SharePoint and OneDrive second; Teams third; all simultaneously
Configuration Impact: Configures location scopes and rollout schedule
Required Participants: Messaging; Collaboration; Change Manager; Business Owners
Default If Undecided: Enforce validated high-risk Exchange and priority repository scenarios before broad expansion
Engineering Notes: Different workloads can require different tuning.

Customer Question: For each data category and destination, should DLP warn, require justification, encrypt, quarantine or block?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines exact production rules and user experience.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Warn for Internal; justify for Confidential; block Highly Confidential externally; encrypt approved partner email
Default If Undecided: Use the least disruptive action that still satisfies the approved risk requirement
Engineering Notes: Keep actions consistent across workloads where service capabilities permit.

Customer Question: Which browser destinations may receive sensitive or labeled data?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines service-domain groups and upload restrictions.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Microsoft 365; approved CRM; client portal; sanctioned storage; blocked personal email and public AI
Default If Undecided: Allow sanctioned business destinations and block high-risk unsanctioned destinations
Engineering Notes: Review destination ownership and authentication.

Customer Question: Which applications may receive sensitive content through clipboard, file-open or process transfer?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines restricted application and process groups.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Microsoft 365 Apps; approved case-management tool; secure editor; prohibited personal applications
Default If Undecided: Allow only governed business applications for sensitive content
Engineering Notes: Avoid broad path-based application exceptions.

Customer Question: Which printers and removable devices qualify as approved destinations for sensitive data?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines printer groups, device identifiers and encryption requirements.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Secure badge printers; department printers; encrypted USB device IDs; no removable media
Default If Undecided: Allow secure managed printers and individually approved encrypted removable devices
Engineering Notes: Assign owners and review dates to approved removable devices.

Customer Question: Which measurable conditions must be met before moving a policy from simulation to enforcement?
Why This Must Be Asked: Creates a repeatable approval gate and prevents premature blocking.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: False positives below 5 percent; no critical workflow failures; training complete; support ready; rollback tested
Configuration Impact: Determines change approval and enforcement timing
Required Participants: Compliance; Change Manager; Business Owners; Service Desk
Default If Undecided: Require accepted simulation results, owner approval, support readiness and rollback documentation
Engineering Notes: An emergency enforcement path should remain separate.

Customer Question: Who resolves conflicts between legal, regulatory, contractual and business retention requirements?
Why This Must Be Asked: Engineers need an authoritative decision when requirements overlap or contradict.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: General Counsel; Records Committee; Compliance Officer; outside counsel
Configuration Impact: Determines retention mapping and unresolved-policy handling
Default If Undecided: Do not implement destructive retention until Legal or Records resolves the conflict
Engineering Notes: Document the controlling authority and rationale.

Customer Question: Which users, sites, teams and mailboxes should receive retention first?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines pilot and production policy scope.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Legal and HR sites first; regulated business units; all mailboxes; all Teams
Configuration Impact: Configures retention locations and implementation waves
Required Participants: Workload Owners; Data Owners; Change Manager
Default If Undecided: Pilot controlled noncritical locations before regulated production scope
Engineering Notes: Use test content and validate propagation timing.

Customer Question: Which directory or site attributes may be trusted to dynamically scope retention?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines adaptive-scope queries and data-quality dependencies.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Department; country; employee type; group membership; site sensitivity; custom property
Default If Undecided: Use static scope until authoritative attributes are demonstrably reliable
Engineering Notes: Define who corrects inaccurate source attributes.

Customer Question: Which users and repositories should see each retention label?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines publication policies and user complexity.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Records team only; legal sites; HR libraries; all users; default library label
Required Participants: Data Owners; Change Manager; Purview Engineer
Default If Undecided: Publish labels only to users and repositories that can apply them correctly
Engineering Notes: Avoid exposing irrelevant record labels tenant-wide.

Customer Question: After content is declared a record, may users continue editing or changing metadata?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines record locking and business workflow behavior.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Locked immediately; metadata only; edit until event; unlock with Records approval
Default If Undecided: Lock finalized regulated records and permit approved metadata changes only where required
Engineering Notes: Test versioning and coauthoring.

Customer Question: How long should proof of disposition and reviewer decisions be retained?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines evidence repository retention and legal defensibility.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Seven years; ten years; permanent; aligned to audit period
Default If Undecided: Retain according to the longest applicable audit or legal requirement
Engineering Notes: Disposition evidence may outlive the disposed content.

Customer Question: Which retention, deletion, hold, record and event scenarios must be validated?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines the test plan and acceptance evidence.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: User deletion; preservation; policy expiration; legal hold; event trigger; disposition review; proof of deletion
Default If Undecided: Test every destructive and preservation scenario used in production
Engineering Notes: Use synthetic content in controlled locations.

Customer Question: Who may create Teams, Microsoft 365 Groups and SharePoint sites?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines self-service creation, provisioning workflow and administrative restrictions.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: All employees; approved creators; administrators only; request workflow
Configuration Impact: Configures group creation and provisioning controls
Default If Undecided: Use an approved creator group or provisioning workflow when governance metadata is required
Engineering Notes: A restricted model needs a prompt request process.

Customer Question: What information must be collected before a workspace is created?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines request form, naming, ownership and lifecycle automation.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Business purpose; primary owner; secondary owner; privacy; sensitivity; external sharing; expiration; department
Default If Undecided: Require purpose, two owners, sensitivity and external-sharing need
Engineering Notes: Use metadata to drive policy and lifecycle decisions.

Customer Question: What prefix, suffix, department, region or project terminology should be included in workspace names?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines Entra naming policy and provisioning logic.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Department-purpose; region-project; classification prefix; no personal names; blocked executive terms
Default If Undecided: Use a consistent business-purpose naming pattern without sensitive classifications in the name
Engineering Notes: Account for system-created and migration-created groups.

Customer Question: After how long should eligible workspaces expire unless an owner renews them?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines Microsoft 365 Group expiration and notifications.
Expected Answer Type: Number of days by workspace type
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: 90; 180; 365 days; no automatic expiration for regulated workspaces
Default If Undecided: Use 180 or 365 days based on activity and require owner renewal
Engineering Notes: Retention does not automatically require the workspace to remain active.

Customer Question: Who may directly invite guests, and who must use a request workflow?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines guest invitation restrictions and operational support.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Approved inviters; site owners; department coordinators; administrators only
Default If Undecided: Use approved inviters or entitlement-management workflows
Engineering Notes: Review invitation authority after role changes.

Customer Question: What expiration period applies to each external-user type, and who may renew access?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines access packages, reviews and guest lifecycle.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Clients 180 days; vendors contract term; one-time users 30 days; partner users one year
Configuration Impact: Configures guest expiration and renewal workflows
Default If Undecided: Use 90-day review and one-year maximum unless renewed
Engineering Notes: Expiration should apply to access assignments as well as account objects where possible.

Customer Question: Should default links use Specific people or organization-only, and should they default to View or Edit?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines final SharePoint and OneDrive sharing defaults.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Specific people and View; organization-only and View; site-specific exception
Default If Undecided: Specific people with View permission
Engineering Notes: Permit site-level exceptions only when documented.

Customer Question: Should denied or unanswered access-review decisions automatically remove access?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines automated removal, escalation and recovery procedures.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Automatically remove denied; escalate unanswered; remove unanswered after second review; manual remediation only
Default If Undecided: Automatically remove denied access and escalate unanswered decisions during initial rollout
Engineering Notes: Validate recovery before enabling automatic removal for nonresponse.

Customer Question: May engineers automatically remove expired, anonymous or unapproved sharing links after owner notice?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines remediation automation and customer impact.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Remove immediately from sensitive sites; 7-day owner notice; report only; owner approval required
Default If Undecided: Remove unapproved anonymous links from sensitive sites and notify owners
Engineering Notes: Preserve evidence of high-risk prior exposure where appropriate.

Customer Question: Which repositories are approved for organization-wide access?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines whether broad groups are remediated or certified as intentional.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Intranet; employee handbook; approved enterprise knowledge base; no sensitive repositories
Default If Undecided: Allow organization-wide access only for owner-certified enterprise publishing repositories
Engineering Notes: Review content sensitivity and search exposure.

Customer Question: Which system is authoritative for application ownership, approval and lifecycle status?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines reconciliation and remediation ownership.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: CMDB; application portfolio; Microsoft Entra; procurement system; governance register
Default If Undecided: Use a governed application register reconciled with Microsoft Entra and Cloud Discovery
Engineering Notes: The authoritative register must include non-Entra SaaS applications.

Customer Question: What maximum lifetime applies to client secrets and certificates?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines application credential policy and rotation alerts.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: No secrets; 90-day secrets; one-year certificates; two-year certificates; federated credentials preferred
Configuration Impact: Configures credential standards and remediation priorities
Default If Undecided: Prefer managed or federated credentials; otherwise use short-lived client secrets and monitored certificates
Engineering Notes: Define emergency rotation procedure.

Customer Question: How many owners must an enterprise application or app registration have?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines ownerless-application remediation and lifecycle reviews.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: One business and one technical owner; two technical owners; one named owner minimum
Default If Undecided: Require at least one business owner and one technical owner for critical applications
Engineering Notes: Owner accounts should be active and monitored.

Customer Question: Which delegated or application permissions require enhanced review or prohibition?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines application risk scoring and consent controls.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Directory.ReadWrite.All; Mail.Read; Files.ReadWrite.All; role management; offline access; application permissions
Default If Undecided: Require enhanced review for tenant-wide, write, directory, mail, file and role-management permissions
Engineering Notes: Application permissions should generally receive more scrutiny than delegated permissions.

Customer Question: Must third-party applications have a verified publisher?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines whether unverified applications are blocked or undergo enhanced review.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Verified publisher required; unverified allowed after security review; internal apps exempt
Configuration Impact: Configures consent policy and risk workflow
Default If Undecided: Require verified publishers for third-party applications unless enhanced review approves an exception
Engineering Notes: Verification does not replace a permission and data-handling review.

Customer Question: May users consent to low-risk applications, or must all applications follow admin approval?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines the final user-consent and admin-consent configuration.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: No user consent; verified low-risk only; selected pilot users; unrestricted
Default If Undecided: Permit only verified publishers and low-impact permissions and require admin review otherwise
Engineering Notes: Provide a usable request process.

Customer Question: How quickly must application consent requests be reviewed?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines reviewer coverage and business expectations.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: One business day; three business days; five business days; emergency review path
Default If Undecided: Use a three-business-day target with expedited review for documented urgent needs
Engineering Notes: A restrictive consent policy without responsive review encourages shadow IT.

Customer Question: After how long without sign-in or token activity should an application be reviewed for retirement?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines stale application reporting and remediation.
Expected Answer Type: Number of days by application type
Default If Undecided: Review applications after 90 days of no activity and validate service dependencies before retirement
Engineering Notes: Noninteractive applications can appear inactive if the wrong telemetry is used.

Customer Question: What criteria make a SaaS service approved, monitored, restricted or blocked?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines Defender for Cloud Apps disposition and procurement workflow.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Risk score; data sensitivity; contract; SSO support; MFA; compliance; business owner
Configuration Impact: Configures sanction state and application register
Default If Undecided: Require ownership, security review and approved terms before sanctioning
Engineering Notes: Risk score alone should not determine approval.

Customer Question: Who may authorize disabling an enterprise application, revoking consent or deleting an app registration?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines decommission workflow and rollback authority.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Business owner; application owner; security; change board; executive sponsor
Default If Undecided: Require business-owner and technical-owner approval except during an active security incident
Engineering Notes: Back up configuration and preserve required data before deletion.

Customer Question: Which laws, regulations, contracts and internal policies should controls be mapped against?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines the compliance matrix and evidence scope.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: HIPAA; PCI DSS; NIST; ISO 27001; SOC 2; customer contracts; cyber-insurance requirements
Default If Undecided: Map only confirmed priority obligations and record others as pending legal review
Engineering Notes: Distinguish mandatory obligations from voluntary frameworks.

Customer Question: Who is accountable, who operates, who collects evidence and who tests each control?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines the control register and segregation of responsibilities.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Security accountable; IT operates; Compliance collects; Internal Audit tests
Required Participants: Security; IT Leadership; Data Governance; Internal Audit
Default If Undecided: Assign a named accountable owner and operator for every priority control
Engineering Notes: Avoid assigning entire departments without a named role.

Customer Question: Which security, administrative, data, AI and user events must be searchable?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines test coverage and identifies licensing gaps.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Role changes; sharing; mailbox access; DLP overrides; labels; records; application consent; Copilot activity
Default If Undecided: Validate all privileged, policy, data-access and AI-governance events supported by deployed services
Engineering Notes: Document unsupported or unlicensed events.

Customer Question: Who may search, export and review audit data?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines role assignments and separation of duties.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Security analysts; compliance investigators; legal; internal audit; no service desk access
Default If Undecided: Restrict search and export to dedicated authorized roles
Engineering Notes: Detailed audit data may reveal sensitive user activity.

Customer Question: Which Compliance Manager assessments should be configured first?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines engineering and evidence effort.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Primary regulator first; cyber-insurance second; contractual framework third
