Default If Undecided: Start with legally or contractually required frameworks
Engineering Notes: Avoid building low-priority assessments without evidence-owner capacity.

Customer Question: How should due dates be assigned based on action risk and effort?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines remediation planning and escalation.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Critical 30 days; high 60 days; medium 90 days; low 180 days
Default If Undecided: Use risk-based due dates and executive escalation for overdue high-risk actions
Engineering Notes: Microsoft-managed actions should be separated from customer actions.

Customer Question: Where should current and historical compliance evidence be stored?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines access control, indexing, retention and confidentiality.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: GRC platform; restricted SharePoint site; legal repository; separate sensitive evidence library
Default If Undecided: Use a restricted governed repository with versioning and retention
Engineering Notes: Separate current evidence from historical audit snapshots.

Customer Question: How long is evidence considered current before it must be refreshed?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines scheduled evidence reviews.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Monthly; quarterly; semiannual; annual; refresh on configuration change
Default If Undecided: Refresh high-volatility technical evidence quarterly and policy evidence annually or after change
Engineering Notes: Historical evidence should remain immutable for its audit period.

Customer Question: What information and approval are required before creating an eDiscovery case?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines request form and authorization control.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Matter number; requester; authority; custodians; data sources; date range; legal basis; approval
Default If Undecided: Require written legal authorization and defined scope
Engineering Notes: Cases should not be created from informal administrator requests.

Customer Question: Which shared mailboxes, Teams, SharePoint sites, groups and applications must be considered during investigations?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines source mapping and preservation playbooks.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Shared mailboxes; project sites; Teams channels; CRM exports; approved connected sources
Required Participants: Application Owners; Collaboration Owner; Records Manager
Default If Undecided: Include Microsoft 365 shared and group resources and document external-source procedures
Engineering Notes: Custodian holds may not automatically cover shared sources.

Customer Question: Who may manage cases, place holds, search, review and export?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines Purview role groups and case membership.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Legal Operations manages; compliance searches; counsel reviews; limited personnel export
Default If Undecided: Separate administration, review and export where practical
Engineering Notes: Case membership must remain limited even when someone holds a broad role.

Customer Question: How often should legal-hold readiness be tested?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines recurring assurance and operational preparedness.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Quarterly; semiannual; annual; after major service changes
Default If Undecided: Test annually and after material architecture or service changes
Engineering Notes: Use controlled test custodians and synthetic content.

Customer Question: Who approves collection queries and estimated result volumes before commitment?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines legal and technical validation checkpoints.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Case attorney; Legal Operations; privacy review above defined volume
Default If Undecided: Require legal approval of query, date range and source scope
Engineering Notes: Preserve each query version.

Customer Question: Will review occur in Microsoft Purview eDiscovery Premium or an external legal-review platform?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines licensing, collection, export and chain-of-custody design.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Purview review sets; external counsel platform; hybrid workflow
Default If Undecided: Use Purview when licensed and suitable; otherwise document secured export to approved external platform
Engineering Notes: Account for duplicate handling and analytics differences.

Customer Question: Who may receive exports, and which secure transfer methods are permitted?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines export encryption, chain of custody and access control.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Internal legal; outside counsel; regulator; encrypted drive; secure portal; managed file transfer
Default If Undecided: Permit only named approved recipients through encrypted managed transfer
Engineering Notes: Require receipt acknowledgment and hash verification.

Customer Question: Which repositories and data domains are in scope for the first Copilot or agent rollout?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines risk-assessment and remediation priorities.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: General employee knowledge; sales; IT documentation; exclude HR, legal and executive initially
Default If Undecided: Begin with well-owned, low-to-moderate sensitivity repositories
Engineering Notes: Licensing a user can expose every resource the user can already access, not only the pilot repository.

Customer Question: What makes a repository authoritative enough for Copilot or agent grounding?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines source approval, quality and review.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Named owner; current content; approved publication process; unique source; defined update cadence
Required Participants: Data Governance; Business Owners; AI Governance
Default If Undecided: Require owner, accuracy, currency, access review and maintenance process
Engineering Notes: A popular repository is not automatically authoritative.

Customer Question: Which permission conditions must be remediated before AI access is approved?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines go-live blockers and remediation waves.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Anyone links; organization-wide access to sensitive data; direct permissions; ownerless sites; stale guests
Default If Undecided: Remediate critical anonymous and broad-access exposure in priority repositories
Engineering Notes: Record accepted residual risk for lower-priority repositories.

Customer Question: After how long without review or update should content be considered stale for AI grounding?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines content-quality reports and remediation.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: One year; two years; content-specific schedule; owner certification overrides age
Default If Undecided: Flag content older than one year for owner review unless the source has a documented longer lifecycle
Engineering Notes: Age does not prove inaccuracy.

Customer Question: Which business and restricted personas must be represented in AI access testing?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines test identities and access matrix.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Executive; ordinary employee; HR; finance; legal; contractor; guest; restricted employee; administrator
Default If Undecided: Test ordinary employees, privileged departments, contractors and unauthorized personas
Engineering Notes: Represent memberships and licenses accurately.

Customer Question: Which direct access, search, Copilot, citation, label and encryption scenarios must pass?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines the AI validation plan and go-live evidence.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Authorized retrieval; unauthorized denial; citation access; encrypted file; restricted site; guest account; removed permission
Default If Undecided: Test positive, negative and permission-change scenarios across priority repositories
Engineering Notes: Validate cited source access, not only generated text.

Customer Question: What measurable conditions must be met before broad Copilot or agent production rollout?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines the formal go-live gate.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: All priority sites owned; no critical anonymous exposure; high-risk permissions remediated; audit validated; incident runbook complete
Customer Decision Owner: Executive Sponsor and AI Governance Owner
Required Participants: Security; Data Governance; Compliance; Service Owner
Default If Undecided: Require all critical controls to pass and document accepted medium or lower residual risks
Engineering Notes: Use phased approval rather than a single unrestricted tenant-wide rollout.

Customer Question: What exactly must a data owner certify before a repository is approved for AI use?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines approval form and recurring review.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Audience; authority; accuracy; sensitive data; external access; permissions; retention; update cadence
Required Participants: Business Data Owners; AI Governance; Security
Default If Undecided: Require certification of ownership, audience, current permissions, data quality and intended AI use
Engineering Notes: Approval should expire after material changes or on a recurring schedule.

Customer Question: Which AI uses are approved, restricted or prohibited?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines acceptable-use policy, training and incident criteria.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Drafting; summarization; code assistance; decision support; no autonomous HR decisions; no unapproved sensitive-data entry
Required Participants: Legal; Privacy; HR; Security; Executive Sponsor
Default If Undecided: Permit productivity assistance with human review and prohibit unsupervised high-impact decisions
Engineering Notes: Address both Microsoft and third-party AI.

Customer Question: How should AI use cases and agents be ranked by risk?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines approval, testing and monitoring requirements.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Low read-only internal assistant; medium sensitive-data assistant; high external action or regulated decision
Configuration Impact: Configures use-case register and governance workflow
Default If Undecided: Use tiers based on data sensitivity, audience, actions, autonomy and business impact
Engineering Notes: Risk tier should be reassessed after material changes.

Customer Question: Which AI-generated decisions, communications or actions require human approval?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines workflow design and prevents unsupervised consequential actions.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: External email; system update; financial decision; HR action; data deletion; customer commitment
Configuration Impact: Configures agent flows and business processes
Default If Undecided: Require human approval for external, financial, personnel, legal or irreversible actions
Engineering Notes: Approval must be technically enforced where possible.

Customer Question: Who may investigate Copilot interactions, and under what authorization?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines audit roles and privacy safeguards.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Security incident only; legal matter; compliance review; privacy approval required
Configuration Impact: Configures audit access and investigation runbook
Default If Undecided: Restrict investigation to authorized security, legal or compliance personnel with documented purpose
Engineering Notes: Do not permit routine prompt browsing by general administrators.

Customer Question: What should happen when sensitive data is referenced in supported Copilot interactions?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines audit, warning, blocking and incident behavior.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Audit Internal; warn Confidential; block Highly Confidential references; alert Security
Customer Decision Owner: Data Security and AI Governance Owners
Default If Undecided: Audit first and enforce only validated high-risk scenarios
Engineering Notes: Source permissions and labels remain primary controls.

Customer Question: Should Copilot interaction records be subject to legal hold and eDiscovery, and for which matters?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines retention, case source mapping and legal procedures.
Expected Answer Type: Yes or No plus matter categories
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: All interactions; regulated users only; case-specific holds; no routine hold
Default If Undecided: Include supported Copilot interactions in case-specific legal and investigation procedures
Engineering Notes: Validate service-specific search and export limitations.

Customer Question: Which environments are required for agent development, testing and production?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines environment isolation, access and deployment path.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Separate development, test and production; department development environments; shared sandbox
Configuration Impact: Configures Power Platform and Copilot Studio environments
Customer Decision Owner: Power Platform and AI Governance Owners
Default If Undecided: Use separate development, test and production environments
Engineering Notes: Production data should not be used in development unless explicitly approved.

Customer Question: Which connectors may exchange data within each environment?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines Power Platform data policies and development restrictions.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Business; nonbusiness; blocked; custom connector review; no social-media connectors
Default If Undecided: Permit approved business connectors and block unreviewed external or consumer connectors
Engineering Notes: Separate read-only retrieval from write-enabled actions.

Customer Question: How many owners must every production agent have?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines ownerless-agent detection and certification.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Primary business owner plus technical owner; two named owners; department owner and backup
Configuration Impact: Configures agent register and publication gate
Default If Undecided: Require a business owner and technical owner
Engineering Notes: Unpublish agents when ownership cannot be reestablished.

Customer Question: Which actions may agents perform automatically, and which require human approval or are prohibited?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines plugin, flow, connector and action configuration.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Read data; draft message; create ticket; update record with approval; prohibit deletion; prohibit payment
Configuration Impact: Configures agent actions and approval steps
Default If Undecided: Allow read-only and drafting actions; require approval for writes; prohibit destructive actions unless explicitly approved
Engineering Notes: Assess each action's recoverability and business impact.

Customer Question: Who may publish an agent to a department or the entire organization?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines publisher roles and publication workflow.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Approved product owner; Power Platform administrator; AI Governance Board approval for tenant-wide publication
Required Participants: Business Owner; Security; Power Platform Administrator
Default If Undecided: Restrict publication to authorized publishers after completed approval
Engineering Notes: Maker access should not automatically provide production publication rights.

Customer Question: How often should agents be recertified?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines periodic review of ownership, data, connectors, actions and use.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Quarterly high risk; semiannual medium; annual low
Default If Undecided: Quarterly for action-enabled or sensitive agents and semiannual for ordinary production agents
Engineering Notes: Material changes should trigger an immediate out-of-cycle review.

Customer Question: Which AI services, users, data types and interaction risks should be monitored?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines notification and workforce-monitoring scope.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Enterprise Copilot; Copilot Studio; sanctioned third-party AI; sensitive-data events; prohibited service use
Default If Undecided: Monitor security and sensitive-data risk in approved enterprise AI; require separate authorization for behavioral monitoring
Engineering Notes: Do not assume all AI services expose equivalent telemetry.

Customer Question: Who may disable an agent, connector, flow, account or AI service during an incident?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines incident-response permissions and escalation.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Security may temporarily disable; AI Governance approves prolonged shutdown; business owner notified
Required Participants: AI Governance; Business Owner; Legal; Power Platform Administrator
Default If Undecided: Permit Security Operations to perform time-limited emergency containment with retrospective governance review
Engineering Notes: Containment must preserve evidence where possible.

Customer Question: What prompt-injection, data-exfiltration or malicious instruction conditions qualify as an incident?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines alert severity and response thresholds.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Unauthorized source retrieval; bypass attempt; credential request; hidden instruction; unauthorized action
Configuration Impact: Configures AI detection and incident classification
Default If Undecided: Treat successful unauthorized access or action as high severity and blocked attempts as reviewable detections
Engineering Notes: Distinguish a harmless malformed prompt from a deliberate bypass attempt.

Customer Question: Which user and operational personas are affected by each Phase 3 control?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines communications, training and support preparation.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: End users; executives; data owners; records reviewers; legal; DLP analysts; administrators; agent makers
Default If Undecided: Map all users who see new prompts plus all roles receiving new responsibilities
Engineering Notes: Include external collaborators where behavior changes.

Customer Question: How much productivity impact, support demand or temporary restriction is acceptable during rollout?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines wave size, pilot duration and rollback thresholds.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: No critical workflow failures; support increase below defined percentage; rollback after defined failed transactions
Required Participants: Business Leaders; Service Desk; Technical Lead
Default If Undecided: Use small pilot waves and pause expansion when critical workflows fail
Engineering Notes: Define measurable stop conditions.

Customer Question: What must each role learn before production rollout?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines role-based courses and practical exercises.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Labels; secure sharing; DLP; retention; legal hold; incident process; Copilot; agent development
Required Participants: Data Governance; Security; Legal; Technical Lead
Default If Undecided: Require task-based training relevant to each role
Engineering Notes: Avoid giving all users administrator-level detail.

Customer Question: Which roles must complete training before receiving access or entering enforcement scope?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines group membership, role assignment and rollout sequencing.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Agent makers before maker access; investigators before case access; users before mandatory labels; owners before certification
Default If Undecided: Require training before privileged, investigative or publication access
Engineering Notes: Define temporary revocation when required training expires.

Customer Question: Who sends launch communications, and who approves security, privacy and legal language?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines delivery schedule and accountable message ownership.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: IT drafts; Communications sends; Legal approves; Executive Sponsor endorses
Default If Undecided: Engineering drafts technical content and customer Communications sends approved messaging
Engineering Notes: Include exact effective dates and support channels.

Customer Question: Who owns and updates support articles for labels, DLP, eDiscovery, Copilot and agents?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines documentation stewardship after implementation.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Service Desk owns user articles; engineering owns technical runbooks; governance owns policy guidance
Required Participants: Technical Lead; Change Manager; Workstream Owners
Default If Undecided: Service Desk owns user-facing articles and engineering owns technical runbooks
Engineering Notes: Knowledge content should be reviewed after material policy changes.

Customer Question: What outcomes indicate successful adoption rather than simple feature usage?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines KPI design and executive reporting.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Training completion; correct label selection; lower oversharing; fewer repeat overrides; active approved Copilot users; certified agents
Required Participants: Governance Owners; Service Manager; Department Leaders
Default If Undecided: Measure responsible use, owner participation, support trends and exception reduction
Engineering Notes: High usage can coexist with poor governance.

Customer Question: Who can approve Phase 3 completion, operational ownership, AI readiness and accepted residual risk?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines the formal phase gate.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Executive Sponsor; Security Owner; Data Governance Owner; Compliance; AI Governance; Service Owner
Required Participants: Technical Lead; Workstream Owners; Service Manager
Default If Undecided: Require business, technical, security, governance and operational approval
Engineering Notes: Deferred controls require owners, interim controls and target dates.

Customer Question: Which security platforms and workloads must be actively monitored?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines which alerts require operational ownership and identifies monitoring gaps.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Entra; Defender for Endpoint; Defender for Identity; Defender for Office 365; Defender for Cloud Apps; Purview; Intune; Azure; third-party security platforms
Configuration Impact: Configures monitoring coverage matrix and alert integrations
Required Participants: Security; Identity; Endpoint; Messaging; Compliance; Azure Owners
Default If Undecided: Monitor all deployed Microsoft security services and document unsupported or unlicensed gaps
Engineering Notes: Every production security platform should have an identified monitoring owner.

Customer Question: How should Microsoft Low, Medium, High and Critical alerts map to customer incident priorities?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines ticket priority, escalation and response targets.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Critical=P1; High=P2; Medium=P3; Low=P4; customer-specific matrix
Configuration Impact: Configures alert routing and ITSM severity mapping
Required Participants: Service Manager; Incident Manager; Executive Sponsor
Default If Undecided: Map Critical to highest incident priority and scale downward
Engineering Notes: Account for business criticality in addition to vendor severity.

Customer Question: How quickly must each alert or incident severity be acknowledged and investigated?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines operational staffing and SLA commitments.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Critical 15 minutes; High 1 hour; Medium 4 business hours; Low next business day
Configuration Impact: Configures ITSM SLA, notifications and escalation
Default If Undecided: Use only response targets supported by the contracted operating model
Engineering Notes: Do not configure 24x7 response expectations when the service is staffed only during business hours.

Customer Question: Which events require action outside normal business hours?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines on-call routing and escalation.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Critical identity compromise; ransomware; confirmed data exfiltration; emergency-account use; high-severity Defender incident
Configuration Impact: Configures after-hours notification and on-call process
Required Participants: Executive Sponsor; Service Manager; Incident Manager
Default If Undecided: Escalate Critical incidents and confirmed high-impact security events after hours
Engineering Notes: Explicitly document events that are notification-only until the next business day.

Customer Question: Which actions may Security Operations perform immediately without additional customer approval?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines how quickly compromised identities and devices can be contained.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Disable account; revoke sessions; isolate device; block application; disable forwarding; remove OAuth grant; no automatic containment
Required Participants: Identity; Endpoint; Messaging; Application Owners; Executive Sponsor
Default If Undecided: Permit temporary containment of confirmed compromised accounts and devices with immediate notification
Engineering Notes: Differentiate temporary containment from destructive remediation.

Customer Question: What conditions cause a security alert to become a formal security incident?
Why This Must Be Asked: Ensures consistent severity, evidence handling and executive escalation.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Confirmed compromise; sensitive data exposure; privileged-account misuse; malware spread; unauthorized administrative change
Required Participants: Legal; Privacy; Executive Sponsor; Service Manager
Default If Undecided: Declare incidents for confirmed compromise, material exposure or high-impact control failure
Engineering Notes: Avoid treating every Defender alert as a formal business incident.

Customer Question: Which incidents require immediate leadership notification?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines communications and escalation paths.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: P1 and Critical; regulated data; executive compromise; material outage; ransomware
Default If Undecided: Notify leadership for Critical incidents or incidents with material operational, legal or data exposure impact
Engineering Notes: Avoid overwhelming leadership with low-level technical alerting.

Customer Question: What incident conditions require Legal, Privacy, HR or Compliance involvement?
Why This Must Be Asked: Security incidents can create reporting, employment or privacy obligations.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Personal data exposure; regulated records; insider activity; employee investigation; contractual breach
Configuration Impact: Configures incident escalation and evidence handling
Default If Undecided: Escalate suspected regulated or personal-data exposure to Legal and Privacy
Engineering Notes: Engineers should not independently determine regulatory notification obligations.

Customer Question: How long must incident evidence be retained?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines storage, Purview, SIEM and evidence-repository retention.
Expected Answer Type: Duration by severity or incident type
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: 1 year; 3 years; 7 years; litigation duration plus defined period
Default If Undecided: Retain according to legal and contractual requirements and at least through incident closure and post-incident review
Engineering Notes: Security telemetry retention and formal incident evidence retention can differ.

Customer Question: How often should security tabletop and technical response exercises occur?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines recurring assurance schedule.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Quarterly; semiannual; annual
Required Participants: Identity; Endpoint; Messaging; Executive Leadership; Legal
Default If Undecided: Conduct at least an annual cross-functional exercise and additional targeted technical tests
Engineering Notes: Rotate scenarios across identity, endpoint, email, data and AI.

Customer Question: What alert volume or false-positive rate should trigger detection tuning?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines when exclusions, thresholds or analytic changes are reviewed.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: More than 10 false alerts weekly; false-positive rate over 10 percent; repeated duplicate tickets
Default If Undecided: Review recurring false positives monthly and tune only with supporting evidence
Engineering Notes: Avoid broad suppression rules that create security blind spots.

Customer Question: How often should joiner, mover and leaver exceptions be reviewed?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines recurring identity-assurance operations.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Weekly; monthly; quarterly
Default If Undecided: Review lifecycle exceptions monthly and termination failures immediately
Engineering Notes: Focus recurring review on exceptions from automated processes.

Customer Question: How quickly should an account that remained active after termination be escalated?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines severity and response behavior.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Immediate Critical; within 15 minutes; same business hour
Default If Undecided: Treat confirmed post-termination active access as High or Critical depending on exposure
Engineering Notes: Do not wait for the monthly identity review.

Customer Question: After how many days without approved activity should accounts be investigated, disabled or removed?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines recurring inactive-account reporting.
Default If Undecided: Use the Phase 1 approved threshold and review it annually
Engineering Notes: Differentiate employees, guests, service identities and emergency accounts.

Customer Question: How frequently should privileged role assignments and eligibility be recertified?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines PIM and manual access-review recurrence.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Monthly Global Administrator; quarterly other privileged roles; semiannual low-impact roles
Default If Undecided: Quarterly access review with monthly review of permanent highest-impact assignments
Engineering Notes: Eligible assignments still represent authorization and should be reviewed.

Customer Question: How often should emergency-access accounts be technically validated?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines scheduled account testing, credential verification and alert testing.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Monthly configuration review; quarterly sign-in test; semiannual credential recovery test
Default If Undecided: Review configuration monthly and conduct an approved monitored test quarterly
Engineering Notes: Avoid uncoordinated break-glass testing.

Customer Question: What percentage of active users must be registered for approved MFA or strong authentication?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines the authentication-health KPI.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: 100 percent administrators; 98 percent employees; approved exceptions excluded
Default If Undecided: Require 100 percent privileged coverage and target 100 percent eligible employee coverage with approved exceptions tracked
Engineering Notes: Do not hide exceptions from the denominator without reporting them separately.

Customer Question: By what date should SMS, voice or other weak authentication methods be eliminated or reduced?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines operational migration targets.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: 90 days; six months; privileged users immediately; retain accessibility exceptions
Default If Undecided: Eliminate weak methods for privileged users first and maintain only approved exceptions
Engineering Notes: Review exceptions at least quarterly.

Customer Question: How quickly should High, Medium and Low identity-risk detections be investigated?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines SOC and identity-team workflow.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: High immediate; Medium same business day; Low recurring review
Default If Undecided: Investigate High immediately and Medium within the business day
Engineering Notes: Automated Conditional Access may already restrict access before manual investigation.

Customer Question: How often should remaining legacy-authentication exceptions be reviewed?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines technical-debt and exception lifecycle.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Monthly; quarterly; at contract renewal
Default If Undecided: Review monthly until eliminated
Engineering Notes: Every exception should have a target retirement date.

Customer Question: How long may a temporary Conditional Access exclusion remain active?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines exception expiration and governance.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: 24 hours; 7 days; 30 days; 90 days
Default If Undecided: Use no more than 30 days without formal reapproval and shorter periods for high-risk controls
Engineering Notes: Emergency accounts are governed separately from temporary exclusions.

Customer Question: How often should Conditional Access configuration be compared with the approved architecture?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines recurring configuration assurance.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Monthly; quarterly; after every material change
Default If Undecided: Review monthly and after every material change
Engineering Notes: Export policy IDs and configurations as evidence.

Customer Question: Should any unplanned emergency-account sign-in automatically become a security incident?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines alert severity and containment.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Yes as Critical; yes as High; investigate before incident declaration
Default If Undecided: Treat every unexpected emergency-account sign-in as a high-priority security incident
Engineering Notes: Include failed sign-in attempts in monitoring.

Customer Question: How long may a corporate device remain unenrolled or partially enrolled?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines remediation targets and access exceptions.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Same day; 24 hours; 3 days; no corporate access until enrolled
Default If Undecided: Require enrollment before normal corporate access and remediate failures within one business day
Engineering Notes: New-device provisioning failures should be separated from existing-device migration issues.

Customer Question: After how many days without check-in should a device be investigated or retired?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines cleanup and inventory accuracy.
Default If Undecided: Investigate after 45 days and retire only after ownership validation
Engineering Notes: Spare and seasonal devices require documented exceptions.

Customer Question: How long may a device remain noncompliant before escalation or retirement?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines remediation, notifications and access handling.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Immediate for critical; 24 hours high; 3 days normal; 7-day maximum
Default If Undecided: Immediately contain high-risk devices and allow up to three days for ordinary compliance failures
Engineering Notes: Coordinate with Conditional Access grace periods.

Customer Question: Which Defender device-risk level should make a device noncompliant?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines Defender-to-Intune compliance integration.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Low only; Medium or below; High blocked
Default If Undecided: Mark devices above Medium risk noncompliant, or use Low risk for highly sensitive populations
Engineering Notes: Select thresholds according to user and resource sensitivity.

Customer Question: What percentage of eligible endpoints must be actively reporting to Defender?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines KPI and remediation threshold.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: 100 percent servers; 98 percent clients; all managed devices
Default If Undecided: Target 100 percent of eligible managed endpoints with documented exceptions reported separately
Engineering Notes: Stale Defender devices should not count as healthy coverage.

Customer Question: How quickly should disabled antivirus, firewall, tamper protection or encryption be remediated?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines ticket severity and automated response.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Antivirus disabled immediately; firewall within 4 hours; encryption within 24 hours
Default If Undecided: Treat disabled endpoint protection as same-day remediation with accelerated action for active threats
Engineering Notes: Some encryption remediation may require maintenance windows.

Customer Question: Which endpoint baseline deviations require immediate remediation versus approved exception?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines configuration assurance and exception workflow.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Critical security settings immediate; usability settings reviewed; customer overlay accepted
Default If Undecided: Immediately remediate security-control drift and require exceptions for deliberate deviations
Engineering Notes: Do not automatically overwrite a valid customer-specific overlay.

Customer Question: How quickly should failed critical security or business applications be remediated?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines application monitoring and escalation.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Security agents 4 hours; critical line-of-business app 1 day; optional app best effort
Default If Undecided: Prioritize security agents and required business applications
Engineering Notes: Optional Company Portal applications should not generate the same severity as mandatory software.

Customer Question: Which platform or combination of platforms is authoritative for vulnerability reporting?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines reconciliation, ownership and reporting.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Defender Vulnerability Management; third-party scanner; RMM; combined view
Default If Undecided: Use the approved vulnerability platform and reconcile with asset inventory
Engineering Notes: Avoid double-counting duplicated vulnerabilities from multiple sources.

Customer Question: How quickly must Critical, High, Medium and Low vulnerabilities be remediated?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines remediation queue and escalation.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Critical 7 days; High 30 days; Medium 60 days; Low 90 days
Required Participants: Infrastructure; Endpoint; Application Owners; Executive Sponsor
Default If Undecided: Use risk-based deadlines with materially exploited Critical vulnerabilities expedited
Engineering Notes: Severity should consider exploitability and business exposure.

Customer Question: How should known exploited or actively exploited vulnerabilities be handled?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines emergency patching and containment.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Patch within 24 or 72 hours; isolate; disable service; apply mitigation
Default If Undecided: Expedite remediation and apply compensating containment when immediate patching is not possible
Engineering Notes: Do not wait for the normal patch cycle.

Customer Question: What device populations belong in pilot, broad and critical update rings?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines rollout speed and blast radius.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: IT pilot; 10 percent early adopters; broad users; executive devices; critical kiosks
Default If Undecided: Use IT and representative early adopters before broad production
Engineering Notes: Include hardware and line-of-business application diversity in the pilot.

Customer Question: How long after release may security and quality updates be deferred?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines Intune deferrals and deadlines.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Pilot 0 to 2 days; broad 7 days; deadline 14 days
Default If Undecided: Use short pilot deferral followed by broad deployment within the approved vulnerability SLA
Engineering Notes: Critical exploited vulnerabilities may bypass normal deferrals.

Customer Question: Which Windows release is the approved organizational target, and how long may older supported versions remain?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines feature-update policy and OS technical debt.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Current enterprise-supported release; one prior release temporarily; 90-day migration
Default If Undecided: Maintain a defined supported target release and remediate devices approaching end of support
Engineering Notes: Application compatibility must be validated before forced upgrade.

Customer Question: Which third-party applications must be centrally patched?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines packaging, RMM and vendor updater workload.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Browsers; PDF readers; Java; Zoom; line-of-business software; security tools
Default If Undecided: Centrally patch high-risk and broadly installed business applications
Engineering Notes: Document vendor-managed applications separately.

Customer Question: Who may approve emergency patching or containment outside normal change windows?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines speed of critical vulnerability response.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Security Director; CIO; Change Manager; on-call incident commander
Default If Undecided: Permit Security and Change leadership to approve emergency remediation with retrospective CAB review
Engineering Notes: Document rollback or containment alternatives.

Customer Question: How long may vulnerability remediation be deferred through an exception?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines risk acceptance and expiration.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Critical 7-day extension; High 30 days; Medium 90 days
Default If Undecided: Require short time-bound exceptions with compensating controls
Engineering Notes: Exceptions should not auto-renew.

Customer Question: How frequently should email threat trends and spoof detections be reviewed?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines messaging-security operational workload.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Daily critical review; weekly threat review; monthly trend report
Default If Undecided: Review actionable threats daily or weekly and trends monthly
Engineering Notes: Align frequency with available staffing.

Customer Question: How long may a temporary sender, domain or URL allow entry remain active?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines Tenant Allow Block List governance.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: 7 days; 30 days; 90 days; permanent only under formal approval
Default If Undecided: Use short-lived exceptions and require revalidation before renewal
Engineering Notes: Permanent broad domain allows should be avoided.

Customer Question: How quickly should reported phishing submissions be reviewed?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines analyst workload and user expectations.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: 15 minutes; 1 hour; 4 business hours; next business day
Default If Undecided: Prioritize suspected phishing within the business day and escalate active campaigns immediately
Engineering Notes: Security awareness simulations should be marked to avoid unnecessary incident handling.

Customer Question: May Defender automatically remove malicious messages or remediate mailboxes?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines automated investigation and response level.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Automatic remediation; analyst approval; executives require approval; no automation
Configuration Impact: Configures Defender automated investigation and Action Center processes
Default If Undecided: Allow supported automatic remediation with operational review for ordinary users and controlled handling for high-impact mailboxes
Engineering Notes: Define undo procedure.

Customer Question: How frequently should anonymous links, external sharing and guest activity be reviewed?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines collaboration-security monitoring.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Weekly sensitive sites; monthly tenant review; quarterly owner certification
Default If Undecided: Review high-risk exposure monthly and sensitive sites more frequently where practical
Engineering Notes: Combine technical exposure metrics with owner certification.

Customer Question: What should happen when a new anonymous link is created?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines monitoring and automated remediation.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Alert only; remove automatically from sensitive sites; create ticket; notify owner
Default If Undecided: Automatically or promptly remove unapproved anonymous links from sensitive sites and notify the owner
Engineering Notes: Public-content sites require an approved exception.

Customer Question: Who may approve operational changes to email and collaboration security policies?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines tuning authority and prevents informal weakening of controls.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Security approves; messaging or collaboration engineer implements; CAB approves user-impacting changes
Default If Undecided: Require Security approval for material protection changes
Engineering Notes: Sender-specific exceptions should not drive tenant-wide weakening.

Customer Question: What percentage of in-scope content should be appropriately labeled?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines KPI thresholds and remediation.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: 95 percent high-value sites; 90 percent email; 100 percent regulated records
Default If Undecided: Track coverage and unlabeled sensitive content rather than requiring an arbitrary universal percentage
Engineering Notes: Auto-generated and unsupported content may require separate treatment.

Customer Question: What should happen when sensitive content is discovered without the expected label?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines remediation workflow.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Auto-label; notify owner; open ticket; quarantine; report only
Default If Undecided: Validate classification and automatically label only where detection accuracy is proven
Engineering Notes: Avoid bulk labeling based on unvalidated classifiers.

Customer Question: How quickly must Critical, High, Medium and Low DLP events be reviewed?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines analyst staffing and incident workflow.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Critical 1 hour; High 4 hours; Medium 1 business day; Low weekly review
Default If Undecided: Review high-risk suspected data exfiltration immediately and lower-risk policy events according to business hours
Engineering Notes: Differentiate policy violations from actual data-loss incidents.

Customer Question: When should repeated DLP overrides trigger an investigation or policy review?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines operational tuning and user follow-up.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: More than 3 overrides weekly; repeated override of same rule; department override rate over 10 percent
Default If Undecided: Review repeated user or rule-specific overrides monthly
Engineering Notes: A high legitimate override rate usually indicates a policy-design problem.

Customer Question: What false-positive rate requires DLP policy retuning?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines when engineers adjust detection conditions.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: 5 percent; 10 percent; any critical workflow false positive
Default If Undecided: Retune when false positives materially disrupt business or exceed the agreed tolerance
Engineering Notes: Do not create broad exclusions solely to improve headline statistics.

Customer Question: How quickly must failed or incorrectly scoped retention policies be investigated?
Why This Must Be Asked: Retention failures can create preservation or premature-deletion risk.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Immediate for potential deletion; same day for missing coverage; five days for reporting problem
Default If Undecided: Immediately escalate failures that could cause unintended deletion or failed legal preservation
Engineering Notes: Treat retention system health differently from general user support.

Customer Question: How long may an item remain pending in disposition review?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines reviewer workload, reminders and escalation.
Default If Undecided: Escalate items pending longer than 30 days or according to the approved records schedule
Engineering Notes: Reviewer departure must trigger reassignment.

Customer Question: Who validates business events that start retention, and how quickly must errors be corrected?
Why This Must Be Asked: Incorrect events can shift deletion dates for entire record sets.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: HR validates termination; Legal validates case closure; Contracts validates expiration
Default If Undecided: Use the authoritative business-process owner to validate events
Engineering Notes: Maintain traceability between source event and Purview event.

Customer Question: How frequently should assessments, overdue actions and evidence freshness be reviewed?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines governance meetings and reporting.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Monthly operational; quarterly executive; annual full assessment
Default If Undecided: Review open actions monthly and report strategic posture quarterly
Engineering Notes: High-risk overdue actions should escalate outside routine cadence.

Customer Question: Which Microsoft 365, Azure, server and application workloads require independent backup?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines backup licensing, architecture and coverage.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Exchange; SharePoint; OneDrive; Teams; Azure VMs; file servers; SQL; application data
Default If Undecided: Protect business-critical data not adequately recoverable through the approved native service model
Engineering Notes: Retention and backup requirements must be considered separately.

Customer Question: How long should backup copies be retained?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines backup-policy retention and storage costs.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: 30 days; 1 year; 7 years; daily-monthly-yearly tiers
Default If Undecided: Retain according to approved recovery need and avoid using backup as an uncontrolled records archive
Engineering Notes: Long backup retention can conflict with data-deletion and privacy requirements.

Customer Question: Who may initiate a mailbox, file, site, server or database restore?
Why This Must Be Asked: Restore capability provides access to sensitive historical data.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Service desk item restore; backup administrator service restore; data-owner approval for bulk restore
Configuration Impact: Configures backup roles and support process
Default If Undecided: Use least-privileged backup roles and require approval for bulk or alternate-location restores
Engineering Notes: Audit restore operations.

Customer Question: Must backups be immutable or otherwise protected from administrative deletion?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines backup architecture and resilience controls.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Immutable for critical systems; immutable for defined days; provider-controlled isolation; no requirement
Default If Undecided: Use immutability or equivalent isolation for critical-recovery copies where supported
Engineering Notes: Define who can alter retention or immutability settings.

Customer Question: How often should item-level and service-level restores be tested?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines assurance schedule and customer effort.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Quarterly item restore; semiannual service restore; annual disaster exercise
Default If Undecided: Test item recovery quarterly and more complex service recovery at least annually
Engineering Notes: Record actual time and issues, not just pass or fail.

Customer Question: How quickly must each critical service or business process be restored?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines recovery architecture and prioritization.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: 1 hour; 4 hours; 8 hours; one business day; best effort
Configuration Impact: Configures RTO targets and recovery planning
Default If Undecided: Require business owners to set service-specific objectives rather than engineers assuming them
Engineering Notes: Distinguish vendor service restoration from customer data restoration.

Customer Question: How much data loss is acceptable for each critical workload?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines backup frequency and recovery architecture.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: 15 minutes; 1 hour; 4 hours; 24 hours
Default If Undecided: Require workload owners to define acceptable data-loss windows
Engineering Notes: Some SaaS backup platforms may not support every requested RPO.

Customer Question: How long may a critical workload remain without successful backup protection?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines backup incident severity and escalation.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Immediate investigation; 4 hours; 24 hours; one backup cycle
Default If Undecided: Escalate failures affecting critical workloads immediately
Engineering Notes: Repeated successful retries can still indicate a reliability problem.

Customer Question: Which AI adoption metrics should be tracked?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines dashboard scope and leadership reporting.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Licensed users; active users; prompts; approved agent users; department adoption; inactive licenses
Required Participants: Executive Sponsor; Licensing Owner; Business Leaders
Default If Undecided: Track active adoption, unused licensing and governed agent usage
Engineering Notes: Usage volume is not itself evidence of business value.

Customer Question: How quickly should sensitive-data or risky AI events be reviewed?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines investigator staffing and incident thresholds.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Critical 1 hour; High 4 hours; Medium 1 business day
Default If Undecided: Prioritize confirmed data exposure and unauthorized agent actions
Engineering Notes: Not every questionable prompt should become a formal incident.

Customer Question: What should happen when use of an unapproved AI service is detected?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines user response, application governance and possible blocking.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Educate; warn; open ticket; block service; investigate data exposure
Default If Undecided: Investigate organizational data exposure and restrict high-risk unapproved AI services
Engineering Notes: Separate accidental access from repeated policy violations.

Customer Question: What should happen when an agent is discovered that is not in the approved inventory?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines unapproved-agent containment and investigation.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Unpublish immediately; notify owner; review within 24 hours; report only
Default If Undecided: Restrict or unpublish unknown broadly available agents pending review
Engineering Notes: Preserve configuration before containment.

Customer Question: How frequently must each agent's purpose, owner and audience be recertified?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines recurring agent governance.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Quarterly high risk; semiannual medium; annual low
Default If Undecided: Quarterly for sensitive or action-enabled agents and semiannual for ordinary production agents
Engineering Notes: Material changes trigger immediate reassessment.

Customer Question: How often should agent connectors and their permissions be reviewed?
Why This Must Be Asked: Connectors may gain permissions or change data destinations over time.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Quarterly for write-enabled or custom; semiannual standard; change-triggered review
Default If Undecided: Review custom and write-enabled connectors quarterly
Engineering Notes: Credential or permission changes should trigger out-of-cycle review.

Customer Question: How often must agent knowledge sources be reviewed for authority, accuracy and permissions?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines source certification and stale-content handling.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Monthly high-change; quarterly standard; annual static policy data
Default If Undecided: Review production agent sources quarterly unless a shorter business lifecycle applies
Engineering Notes: A source can remain technically available while becoming operationally obsolete.

Customer Question: Who may immediately unpublish an agent, disable a connector, revoke credentials or restrict an audience?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines incident-response speed and permissions.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Security Operations temporary containment; AI Governance prolonged disablement; business owner consulted
Required Participants: AI Governance; Power Platform Administrator; Business Owner
Default If Undecided: Allow temporary security containment of confirmed high-risk activity
Engineering Notes: Preserve current agent version and evidence before changes where practical.

Customer Question: What constitutes reportable or material AI-related data exposure?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines incident severity, legal escalation and evidence handling.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Unauthorized user received data; regulated data exposed; external destination; credential disclosure
Default If Undecided: Escalate any confirmed unauthorized disclosure of sensitive or regulated data
Engineering Notes: Engineers should not determine external notification obligations without Legal.

Customer Question: What false-positive or business-impact threshold requires AI DLP retuning?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines operational tuning cadence.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: False positives above 5 percent; repeated blocked approved workflow; defined number of overrides
Customer Decision Owner: Data Security and AI Governance Owners
Default If Undecided: Retune when validated false positives materially affect legitimate workflows
Engineering Notes: Do not broadly exclude data or users to resolve isolated issues.

Customer Question: How frequently should AI retention requirements be reassessed?
Why This Must Be Asked: AI services and legal requirements may change rapidly.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Quarterly; semiannual; annual; after material regulatory change
Default If Undecided: Review annually and after material legal or service changes
Engineering Notes: Changes require legal and privacy review.

Customer Question: What changes require the agent to be formally reassessed and reapproved?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines change-control and risk-review triggers.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: New connector; write action; new data source; broader audience; ownership change; prompt redesign; new external endpoint
Default If Undecided: Treat connector, action, data-source and audience changes as material
Engineering Notes: Cosmetic text changes can use a lighter change path.

Customer Question: Which team owns Level 1, Level 2 and engineering escalation for each Secure Plus service?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines ticket routing and operational accountability.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Service desk L1; Modern Work L2; Security L2; Engineering L3; vendor L4
Required Participants: Technical Lead; Workstream Owners; Service Desk
Default If Undecided: Service desk performs triage and routes specialized controls to workload owners
Engineering Notes: Document out-of-scope support scenarios.

Customer Question: Which recurring requests should have standardized request forms and approvals?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines operational consistency and automation opportunities.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Guest access; CA exception; DLP exception; app consent; BitLocker recovery; agent request; site request
Required Participants: Security; Identity; Data Governance; Application Owners
Default If Undecided: Standardize recurring privileged, access and exception requests
Engineering Notes: Capture the information engineers need to fulfill the request safely.

Customer Question: When should recurring incidents become a formal problem-management item?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines root-cause investigation and engineering backlog behavior.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Three similar incidents in 30 days; repeated policy failure; recurring outage; repeated exception request
Default If Undecided: Create a problem when incidents indicate a recurring systemic issue
Engineering Notes: Do not repeatedly resolve the same symptom without engineering review.

Customer Question: Which recurring Secure Plus changes can be preapproved as standard changes?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines administrative efficiency while preserving governance.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Add user to approved pilot group; update existing approved app; routine patch ring; emergency exception removal
Default If Undecided: Keep high-impact Conditional Access, DLP, retention and AI policy changes under normal formal change
Engineering Notes: Standard changes still need logging and validation.

Customer Question: Who receives the monthly Secure Plus service report?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines report detail, confidentiality and distribution.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: CIO; IT Director; Security; Compliance; Operations; account team
Default If Undecided: Send detailed technical report to operational stakeholders and summarized risk view to leadership
Engineering Notes: Security findings may require restricted distribution.

Customer Question: Which KPIs must appear in operational and executive reports?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines dashboard and data collection scope.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Incidents; MFA coverage; privileged assignments; device compliance; vulnerabilities; phishing; DLP; sharing; AI usage; exceptions
Default If Undecided: Include security posture, operational health, risk backlog, compliance exceptions and roadmap status
Engineering Notes: Trend and target are more useful than isolated point-in-time values.

Customer Question: Which risks, incidents or service conditions must be explicitly highlighted to leadership?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines leadership visibility and escalation.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Critical incidents; overdue High risks; security coverage under target; expired exceptions; failed recovery tests
Default If Undecided: Highlight Critical events, overdue High risks and material control failures
Engineering Notes: Avoid overwhelming leadership with every technical finding.

Customer Question: How frequently should runbooks, diagrams and inventories be reviewed?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines operational documentation cadence.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Runbooks quarterly; inventories monthly; diagrams semiannual; emergency procedures quarterly
Default If Undecided: Review runbooks quarterly, inventories monthly or quarterly and architecture after material changes
Engineering Notes: High-risk emergency procedures should be reviewed more frequently.

Customer Question: Who owns updating engineering runbooks and architecture documentation after production changes?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines whether documentation remains operationally current.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Implementing engineer updates; architect approves; service owner reviews
Default If Undecided: Implementing engineer updates technical documentation before change closure
Engineering Notes: A production change is incomplete until relevant documentation is updated.

Customer Question: How frequently should operational and executive service reviews occur?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines governance meeting calendar.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Monthly operational; quarterly executive; semiannual roadmap
Default If Undecided: Monthly operational and quarterly executive reviews
Engineering Notes: Separate operational troubleshooting from executive decisions.

Customer Question: How often should production settings be compared with the approved Secure Plus Golden Baseline?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines recurring drift assessment and engineering workload.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Monthly; quarterly; semiannual; annual
Default If Undecided: Perform quarterly comprehensive assessment with more frequent checks for critical controls
Engineering Notes: Critical controls such as CA and privileged access may warrant monthly checks.

Customer Question: May engineers automatically restore a drifted setting to baseline, or is customer approval required?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines remediation automation and change requirements.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Auto-remediate critical controls; ticket and approve; report only; emergency security remediation allowed
Required Participants: Technical Lead; Change Manager; Workload Owners
Default If Undecided: Create a ticket and validate intentional changes before remediation; permit emergency correction of severe security drift under approved authority
Engineering Notes: Do not overwrite valid customer-specific configurations.

Customer Question: How frequently should critical controls be technically tested rather than only configuration-checked?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines operating-effectiveness testing.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Quarterly CA tests; annual recovery; semiannual DLP; annual eDiscovery; quarterly emergency account
Default If Undecided: Test high-risk access and emergency controls quarterly and complete broader assurance annually
Engineering Notes: A correct configuration export does not prove the control functions.

Customer Question: Who may accept a deviation from the Golden Baseline?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines risk acceptance and variance governance.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Control owner Low; Security Medium; executive High or Critical
Default If Undecided: Require executive approval for High or Critical baseline deviations
Engineering Notes: Technical engineers should not self-approve risk exceptions.

Customer Question: How long may baseline exceptions remain before mandatory reapproval?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines exception expiration and recurring review.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: 30 days High; 90 days Medium; one year Low
Default If Undecided: Use short time-bound exceptions and require reassessment before renewal
Engineering Notes: Avoid indefinite exceptions.

Customer Question: How frequently should residual risks be reviewed?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines risk-register governance.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Monthly Critical or High; quarterly Medium; annual Low
Default If Undecided: Review High risks monthly and all open risks quarterly
Engineering Notes: Material environment changes can trigger out-of-cycle review.

Customer Question: When should an overdue remediation item be escalated to leadership?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines accountability and governance.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Any overdue Critical; High more than 30 days; repeated due-date extension
Default If Undecided: Escalate overdue Critical and High risks at the next governance review or immediately when material
Engineering Notes: Due-date changes require renewed ownership and risk acceptance.

Customer Question: What happens when a security or baseline exception expires without renewal?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines whether access or configuration automatically returns to standard.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Automatically restore baseline; disable exception; escalate and retain temporarily; block affected workflow
Default If Undecided: Return to baseline unless a formally approved renewal exists
Engineering Notes: Notify owners before expiration.

Customer Question: How should new improvements compete with existing security debt, projects and business initiatives?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines quarterly roadmap decisions.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Risk reduction; compliance requirement; business value; support reduction; Microsoft deprecation; AI enablement
Default If Undecided: Prioritize critical risk, required compliance and Microsoft deprecations before optimization work
Engineering Notes: Use consistent scoring across workstreams.

Customer Question: What types of Microsoft service changes require engineering review or a formal customer change?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines Message Center triage and configuration-maintenance process.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Deprecation; default change; security baseline update; licensing change; new feature; user-impacting UI change
Default If Undecided: Formally review changes affecting security, licensing, integrations, user behavior or deprecated functionality
Engineering Notes: Not every Message Center post requires a project change.

Customer Question: How long may unsupported systems, legacy authentication, unmanaged applications and other technical debt remain?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines roadmap escalation and exception treatment.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: 30 days Critical; 90 days High; one year strategic dependency
Default If Undecided: Require owner, business reason, compensating control and retirement date
Engineering Notes: Technical debt without a target state becomes permanent risk.

Customer Question: How should new Copilot and agent opportunities be proposed, assessed and prioritized?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines AI roadmap and prevents unmanaged production adoption.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Business use-case form; data-owner review; risk tier; ROI; security assessment
Default If Undecided: Require business purpose, owner, data sources, audience and risk assessment before production development
Engineering Notes: Separate experimentation from production use.

Customer Question: How often should security, data, collaboration, application and AI governance policies be formally reviewed?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines governance calendar.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Annual; semiannual high-risk; after regulatory change
Default If Undecided: Perform formal annual review and out-of-cycle review after material legal or architectural changes
Engineering Notes: Record policy version and approval date.

Customer Question: How often should the target-state architecture be reassessed?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines architectural governance and modernization planning.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Annual; semiannual; after acquisition; after major Microsoft platform change
Required Participants: Security; Infrastructure; Data; Application; AI Owners
Default If Undecided: Review annually and after material environment changes
Engineering Notes: Architecture review should identify opportunities to remove legacy dependencies.

Customer Question: How frequently should administrative, application, data, site and agent ownership be recertified?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines owner-review automation and governance effort.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Quarterly privileged roles; semiannual agents and sites; annual applications and data domains
Required Participants: Identity; Application; Data; Collaboration; AI Owners
Default If Undecided: Quarterly for privileged ownership and semiannual for high-risk business objects
Engineering Notes: Owner departure should trigger immediate review rather than waiting for scheduled certification.

Customer Question: Who can approve a change to the standard Secure Plus Golden Baseline?
Why This Must Be Asked: The reusable standard must not change merely because one customer has a justified exception.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Architecture board; security leadership; technical standards committee; service owner
Customer Decision Owner: Technical Lead or Security Architecture Owner
Default If Undecided: Require technical and security architecture approval for standard-baseline changes
Engineering Notes: Customer-specific deviations belong in the variance register, not the standard baseline.

Customer Question: How should approved customer deviations from the Secure Plus standard be documented and reviewed?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines separation between the reusable baseline and customer configuration.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Customer overlay; exception register; architecture decision record; risk acceptance
Required Participants: Customer Security Owner; Risk Owner; Workstream Leads
Default If Undecided: Maintain each customer deviation separately with rationale, owner and review date
Engineering Notes: Do not modify the standard baseline to match a single customer's exception.

Customer Question: What must be included in the annual Secure Plus assurance assessment?
Why This Must Be Asked: Determines the depth of the annual review and associated engineering effort.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: Identity; MFA; PIM; CA; Intune; Defender; email; collaboration; Purview; backup; Copilot; agents; governance
Required Participants: Technical Lead; Compliance; Service Manager; Workstream Owners
Default If Undecided: Assess all applicable Golden Baseline controls, validate critical controls technically and review all active exceptions
Engineering Notes: Mark controls as not applicable only through an approved architecture decision.

Customer Question: What findings prevent the environment from passing the annual Secure Plus assurance review?
Why This Must Be Asked: Defines a meaningful pass or fail condition rather than simply producing a gap report.
Suggested Answer Options or Examples: No open Critical findings; no expired High exceptions; required control coverage above target; all break-glass tests successful
Configuration Impact: Configures assurance scoring and remediation gate
Required Participants: Executive Sponsor; Risk Owner; Technical Lead
Default If Undecided: No open Critical findings, no expired high-risk exceptions and no failed foundational identity or recovery controls
Engineering Notes: Other findings should remain visible in the improvement roadmap rather than being hidden to achieve a passing score.
